```{r loading files 08262025}
#import merged phenotype file 
nmsu23_nor_pheno <- read.csv("2023/MSI_data/Output_files/nmsu23_nor_combined_filtered_phenotypes_MSI.csv", sep = ",") %>% 
  select(-X) # remove index column
colnames(nmsu23_nor_pheno)
# Before running models, make sure the variables are in correct form. Need to convert into factors and numeric if needed.
  # converting all factorial variables into factor
nmsu23_nor_pheno[, c("Range", "Rep","Germplasm","Plot", "Row")] <- lapply(nmsu23_nor_pheno[, c("Range", "Rep","Germplasm","Plot", "Row")], as.factor)

#import genotype file
grm_aa <- read.csv("2022/genotype_data/grm_final.csv", sep = ",", row.names = 1)
grm_aa <- as.matrix(grm_aa)
mean(diag(grm_aa)) # 1
hist(diag(grm_aa))

grm_agh <- grm_aa+diag(.0005,length(grm_aa[,1]),length(grm_aa[,1])) # adding 0.05 nugget/ridge to ensure matrix is strictly positive definite
grm_inverse <- solve(grm_agh)

```


Normally if the range of numbers vary a lot between vi's and yield, then we can scale yield to variance level of vi's. but here since yield is in lb and upto 2 digit, should have that issue. If got any, we can always use scaled yield.
```{r scaling yield to its closest flight variance}
# we only have to scale 6 harvest values based on gndvi's value. Of course the variance between VI's differ but it should be okay to use Yield scaled onto gndvi for analysis with NDRE and Ggndvi as well. 

# Define the mapping of yield traits to gndvi columns
yield_traits <- paste0("yld", 2:7)
gndvi_times <- c("GNDVI_152", "GNDVI_179", "GNDVI_201", "GNDVI_242", "GNDVI_278", "GNDVI_307") # selecting one of the time point closest to each harvest bcz we will fit those two in the models below. 

# Loop over each yield trait
for (i in 1:length(yield_traits)) {
  
  trait <- yield_traits[i]
  gndvi_col <- gndvi_times[i]
  
  # Calculate variance of gndvi and yield
  gndvi_var <- var(nmsu23_nor_pheno[[gndvi_col]], na.rm = TRUE)
  yld_var <- var(nmsu23_nor_pheno[[trait]], na.rm = TRUE)
  
  # Calculate scaling factor
  sf <- sqrt(gndvi_var) / sqrt(yld_var)
  
  # Create new scaled yield column
  new_col <- paste0("sca_", trait)
  nmsu23_nor_pheno[[new_col]] <- nmsu23_nor_pheno[[trait]] * sf
  
  #  Print scaling factor
  cat("Scaling factor for", trait, "using", gndvi_col, ":", sf, "\n")
}


# thus all scaled yields are added as a new column at last. 
```



## Details on RR model explanation in 2022 script
### PEE from manual script based model
Legendre polynomials are the values of the Legendre polynomials at specific time points (or GDDs).

- PEE = Legendre Polynomial Intercept ( which is 1 from Phi matrix) * Plot Level Coefficients for Intercept   + Legendre Polynomial Slope/Linear for harvest date or last imaging event ( which is some number from Phi matrix) * Plot Level Coefficients for slope/Linear

- i.e. PEE = LP intercept × plot intercept coefficient + LP slope × plot slope coefficient [for linear curve]

Random Regression models estimate a covariance matrix of random regression coefficients (K matrix). This matrix must be positive definite (all eigenvalues > 0). Assumes change in covariance pattern across time (opposed to Repeatability model with constant variance)

Repeatability model assumption: same genetic or plot effect at all time points, i.e. constant variance ( cor between time points = 1)




############################  Permanent Environmental Effect ############################      
########   04272026

- Lets use PEE as regressor and compare with no spatial and spatial (autoregressive) model
- now lets use above extracted blups spatial matrix as PEE and fit as a regressor in the model
PEE = intercept + GDD * linear
Eg. 
Phi in harvest 1.
    LPInt      LPLin
62      1 -1.7320508
76      1 -0.7994081
90      1  0.1332347
96      1  0.5329387
104     1  1.0658774
114     1  1.7320508

Then PEE for harvest = 1* Intercept from spatial blups + 1.732 (from 114th GDD) * Linear from spatial blups

### 2. GEER
 - NOTE: yld#, PEE_###, Check AR model (full or 1D)

```{r GEER between all rep combinations for yld2 Nor 2023, 04272026}
### ---------------------------------------------------------
### 1. Function: Fit model and extract genomic BLUPs
### ---------------------------------------------------------
get_gblup_yld2_nor23 <- function(dat, model_type = c("base", "spa", "pee"), grm_inverse) {
  
  # Ensure GRM is treated as inverse relationship matrix
  attr(grm_inverse, "INVERSE") <- TRUE
  
  # Match model type argument
  model_type <- match.arg(model_type)

  # ---------------------------------------------------------
  # Fit model (robust to failure)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------
  fit <- tryCatch({
    
    if (model_type == "base") {
      # Baseline genomic model (no spatial/environmental correction)
      asreml(
        fixed   = yld2 ~ 1 , # we dont need rep here cz the data is only for one rep
        random  = ~ vm(Germplasm, grm_inverse),
        residual= ~ id(units),
        data    = dat
      )
      
    } else if (model_type == "spa") {
      # Genomic model + 2D autoregressive spatial structure
      asreml(
        fixed   = yld2 ~ 1 , # we dont need rep here cz the data is only for one rep
        random  = ~ vm(Germplasm, grm_inverse) + ar1(Row):ar1(Range),
        residual= ~ id(units),
        data    = dat
      )
      
    } else if (model_type == "pee") {
      # Genomic model + permanent environmental effect (PEE)
      asreml(
        fixed   = yld2 ~ 1 + PEE_153,
        random  = ~ vm(Germplasm, grm_inverse),
        residual= ~ id(units),
        data    = dat
      )
    }
    
  }, error = function(e) NULL)   # Return NULL if model fails

  # If model fitting failed → skip
  if (is.null(fit)) return(NULL)

  # ---------------------------------------------------------
  # Extract genomic BLUPs (u_a)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------
  blup <- tryCatch(coef(fit)$random, error = function(e) NULL)
  
  # If extraction failed → skip
  if (is.null(blup)) return(NULL)

  # Keep only Germplasm effects
  blup <- blup[grep("Germplasm", rownames(blup)), , drop = FALSE]
  
  # If no genetic effects found → skip
  if (nrow(blup) == 0) return(NULL)

  # Convert to named numeric vector
  out <- blup[, 1]
  names(out) <- rownames(blup)

  return(out)
}


### ---------------------------------------------------------
### 2. Function: Compute GEER across all replicate pairs
### ---------------------------------------------------------
geer_all_pairs_yld2_nor23 <- function(dat, grm_inverse, rep_col = "Rep") {
  
  # Split dataset by replicate
  rep_list <- split(dat, dat[[rep_col]])
  rep_names <- names(rep_list)
  
  # All pairwise replicate combinations
  pairs <- combn(rep_names, 2, simplify = FALSE)

  # Loop over replicate pairs
  res <- lapply(pairs, function(p) {
    
    d1 <- rep_list[[p[1]]]
    d2 <- rep_list[[p[2]]]

    models <- c("base", "spa", "pee")

    # Compute GEER for each model
    pair_res <- lapply(models, function(m) {
      
      g1 <- get_gblup_yld2_nor23(d1, m, grm_inverse)
      g2 <- get_gblup_yld2_nor23(d2, m, grm_inverse)

      # Skip if either replicate failed
      if (is.null(g1) || is.null(g2)) return(NULL)

      # Align common germplasm entries
      common_ids <- intersect(names(g1), names(g2))
      if (length(common_ids) < 2) return(NULL)

      # Compute correlations
      pear <- tryCatch(
        cor(g1[common_ids], g2[common_ids]),
        error = function(e) NA_real_
      )
      
      spear <- tryCatch(
        cor(g1[common_ids], g2[common_ids], method = "spearman"),
        error = function(e) NA_real_
      )

      # Return results
      data.frame(
        Rep1 = p[1],
        Rep2 = p[2],
        Model = m,
        N_common = length(common_ids),
        Pearson = pear,
        Spearman = spear,
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      )
    })

    do.call(rbind, pair_res)
  })

  # Combine all results
  res <- do.call(rbind, res)
  rownames(res) <- NULL

  return(res)
}


### ---------------------------------------------------------
### 3. Run GEER analysis
### ---------------------------------------------------------
GEER_results_yld2_nor23 <- geer_all_pairs_yld2_nor23(
  nmsu23_nor_pheno,
  grm_inverse
)

GEER_results_yld2_nor23


### ---------------------------------------------------------
### 4. Summary statistics
### ---------------------------------------------------------

# Number of valid comparisons per model
table(GEER_results_yld2_nor23$Model)

# Mean GEER per model
aggregate(
  cbind(Pearson, Spearman) ~ Model,
  GEER_results_yld2_nor23,
  mean
)


### ---------------------------------------------------------

### ---------------------------------------------------------

# Ensure consistent ordering for plotting
GEER_results_yld2_nor23$Model <- factor(
  GEER_results_yld2_nor23$Model,
  levels = c("base", "spa", "pee"),
  labels = c("Base", "Spa(AR)", "PEE"))

# Boxplot of Pearson GEER
boxplot(
  Pearson ~ Model,
  data = GEER_results_yld2_nor23,
  col = c("grey70", "skyblue", "tomato"),
  border = "black",
  ylab = "GEER (Pearson correlation)",
  xlab = "Model",
  main = "Genotypic Effect Estimation across Replicates (GEER)\nHarvest 2, NOR 2023",
  outline = TRUE
)

# Overlay individual replicate-pair estimates
stripchart(
```

###  Spatially Corrected Rep-wise Yield Correlation (SCRYC)
 - correlation of phenotypes/yield after removing spatial effects across reps
- PEE much better cz autoreg.is not capturing
```{r  Spatially Corrected Yiled, Yld2, 04272026}
# ============================================================
# NEW METRIC: SPATIALLY CORRECTED YIELD (yld2_nor23)
# ============================================================

# -------------------------------
# 1. PREPARE WORKING DATA
# -------------------------------
nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC <- nmsu23_nor_pheno

# ============================================================
# 1.1 SPATIAL (AR1): EXTRACT + ALIGN SPATIAL BLUPS
# ============================================================

# Extract all random effects
spa_blup_yld2_nor23 <- uni_nmsu23_nor_yld2_spa$coefficients$random
spa_blup_yld2_nor23
# Extract ONLY Row:Range spatial effects (correct pattern)
spa_eff_yld2_nor23 <- spa_blup_yld2_nor23[
  grep("^Row_[0-9]+:Range_[0-9]+", rownames(spa_blup_yld2_nor23)),
  , drop = FALSE]
spa_eff_yld2_nor23

# Build lookup table (use column name "effect")
spa_df_yld2_nor23 <- data.frame(
  RowRange = rownames(spa_eff_yld2_nor23),
  spa_eff_yld2_nor23 = spa_eff_yld2_nor23[,"effect"],
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
spa_df_yld2_nor23
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Create matching key in phenotype data
# ------------------------------------------------------------
nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$RowRange <- paste0(
  "Row_", nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$Row,
  ":Range_", nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$Range)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Match WITHOUT reordering (IMPORTANT)
# ------------------------------------------------------------

match_idx <- match(
  nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$RowRange,
  spa_df_yld2_nor23$RowRange)

nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$spa_eff_yld2_nor23 <- 
  spa_df_yld2_nor23$spa_eff_yld2_nor23[match_idx]
 # i doubled check the spatial blups and these columns to make sure i am getting what i wanted

# Sanity check (must be zero)
sum(is.na(nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$spa_eff_yld2_nor23)) # 0

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Corrected yield (AR1)
# ------------------------------------------------------------

nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$yld2_spa_corr_nor23 <- 
  nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$yld2 - nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$spa_eff_yld2_nor23




# ============================================================
# 1.2 PEE: DIRECT SPATIAL CORRECTION
# ============================================================

 # we need to scale PEE to be able to use it for spatial correction

# lets see
# Extract coefficient
beta_pee_yld2_nor23 <- uni_nmsu23_nor_yld2_pee$coefficients$fixed["PEE_153", "effect"]
beta_pee_yld2_nor23   #  

# Apply correct spatial correction
nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$yld2_pee_corr_nor23 <- 
  nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$yld2 - 
  beta_pee_yld2_nor23 * nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$PEE_153


# ============================================================
# 2. REP-WISE CORRELATIONS
# ============================================================

# -------------------------------
# SPLIT DATA BY REP
# -------------------------------

rep1_yld2_nor23 <- nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC[nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$Rep == 1, ]
dim(nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC) # 144*73
dim(rep1_yld2_nor23) # should be 144/4 = 36 and it is. JUST SANITY CHECK
rep2_yld2_nor23 <- nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC[nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$Rep == 2, ]
rep3_yld2_nor23 <- nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC[nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$Rep == 3, ]
rep4_yld2_nor23 <- nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC[nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$Rep == 4, ]

# Align by genotype
rep1_yld2_nor23 <- rep1_yld2_nor23[order(rep1_yld2_nor23$Germplasm), ]
rep2_yld2_nor23 <- rep2_yld2_nor23[order(rep2_yld2_nor23$Germplasm), ]
rep3_yld2_nor23 <- rep3_yld2_nor23[order(rep3_yld2_nor23$Germplasm), ]
rep4_yld2_nor23 <- rep4_yld2_nor23[order(rep4_yld2_nor23$Germplasm), ]


# ============================================================
# 1. RAW YIELD
# ============================================================

cor_raw_yld2_nor23 <- c(
  cor(rep1_yld2_nor23$yld2, rep2_yld2_nor23$yld2, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep1_yld2_nor23$yld2, rep3_yld2_nor23$yld2, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep1_yld2_nor23$yld2, rep4_yld2_nor23$yld2, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep2_yld2_nor23$yld2, rep3_yld2_nor23$yld2, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep2_yld2_nor23$yld2, rep4_yld2_nor23$yld2, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep3_yld2_nor23$yld2, rep4_yld2_nor23$yld2, use="complete.obs") )

df_raw_yld2_nor23 <- data.frame(
  Model = "Raw",
  Correlation = cor_raw_yld2_nor23)
df_raw_yld2_nor23

# ============================================================
# 2. AR1 CORRECTED
# ============================================================

cor_spa_cor_yld2_nor23 <- c(
  cor(rep1_yld2_nor23$yld2_spa_corr_nor23, rep2_yld2_nor23$yld2_spa_corr_nor23, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep1_yld2_nor23$yld2_spa_corr_nor23, rep3_yld2_nor23$yld2_spa_corr_nor23, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep1_yld2_nor23$yld2_spa_corr_nor23, rep4_yld2_nor23$yld2_spa_corr_nor23, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep2_yld2_nor23$yld2_spa_corr_nor23, rep3_yld2_nor23$yld2_spa_corr_nor23, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep2_yld2_nor23$yld2_spa_corr_nor23, rep4_yld2_nor23$yld2_spa_corr_nor23, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep3_yld2_nor23$yld2_spa_corr_nor23, rep4_yld2_nor23$yld2_spa_corr_nor23, use="complete.obs"))

df_spa_yld2_nor23 <- data.frame(
  Model = "Spa(AR1)",
  Correlation = cor_spa_cor_yld2_nor23)
df_spa_yld2_nor23

# ============================================================
# 3. PEE CORRECTED
# ============================================================

cor_pee_cor_yld2_nor23 <- c(
  cor(rep1_yld2_nor23$yld2_pee_corr_nor23, rep2_yld2_nor23$yld2_pee_corr_nor23, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep1_yld2_nor23$yld2_pee_corr_nor23, rep3_yld2_nor23$yld2_pee_corr_nor23, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep1_yld2_nor23$yld2_pee_corr_nor23, rep4_yld2_nor23$yld2_pee_corr_nor23, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep2_yld2_nor23$yld2_pee_corr_nor23, rep3_yld2_nor23$yld2_pee_corr_nor23, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep2_yld2_nor23$yld2_pee_corr_nor23, rep4_yld2_nor23$yld2_pee_corr_nor23, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep3_yld2_nor23$yld2_pee_corr_nor23, rep4_yld2_nor23$yld2_pee_corr_nor23, use="complete.obs"))

df_pee_yld2_nor23 <- data.frame(
  Model = "PEE",
  Correlation = cor_pee_cor_yld2_nor23)
df_pee_yld2_nor23

# ============================================================
# 4. COMBINE + PLOT
# ============================================================

df_all_yld2_nor23 <- rbind(
  df_raw_yld2_nor23,
  df_spa_yld2_nor23,
  df_pee_yld2_nor23)

df_all_yld2_nor23$Model <- factor(
  df_all_yld2_nor23$Model,
  levels = c("Raw", "Spa(AR1)", "PEE"))

boxplot(
  Correlation ~ Model,
  data = df_all_yld2_nor23,
  col = c("lightgray", "lightblue", "lightgreen"),
  ylab = "Rep-to-rep correlation",
  main = "nor23 yld2: Spatial Correction Comparison",
  ylim = c(0,1)
)

# Summary
aggregate(Correlation ~ Model, df_all_yld2_nor23, mean)
aggregate(Correlation ~ Model, df_all_yld2_nor23, sd)
```

```{r Combined chunk for harvest3 using Random Regression 04282026}
# ---------- PART 0: Manange data file -----------

#  Manage data file: First, assign harvest based on GDD
# first make harvest3 only data file
nmsu23_nor_pheno_gndvi_only_long_harvestwise <- 
  nmsu23_nor_pheno_gndvi_only_long %>%
  mutate(Harvest = case_when(
    # no harvest 1 in this treatment
    GDD >= 119 & GDD <= 153 ~ "Harvest2", # here upper limit is of actual yld
    GDD >= 153 & GDD <= 181 ~ "Harvest3",
    GDD >= 181 & GDD <= 207 ~ "Harvest4",
    GDD >= 207 & GDD <= 243 ~ "Harvest5",
    GDD >= 243 & GDD <= 279 ~ "Harvest6",
    GDD >= 279 & GDD <= 310 ~ "Harvest7"
  ))

  filter(Harvest == "Harvest3") # !!! capital H

# create factor + numeric GDD
nmsu23_nor_gdd_harvest3$GDD_fac <- as.factor(nmsu23_nor_gdd_harvest3$GDD)

unique(nmsu23_nor_gdd_harvest3$GDD_fac) # 160 165 173 179 181(for yld3)

# Build Legendre basis
unique_gdd_yld3 <- sort(unique(nmsu23_nor_gdd_harvest3$GDD))
unique_gdd_yld3 <- as.numeric(unique_gdd_yld3)

 ######## fitting linear equation
M_yld3 <- stdtime(unique_gdd_yld3, 1) # for linear, 1
lambda_yld3 <- Legendre(1, gengler=TRUE) # for linear, 1 (intercept + slope)

Phi_yld3 <- M_yld3 %*% t(lambda_yld3)
colnames(Phi_yld3) <- c("LPInt", "LPLin")
rownames(Phi_yld3) <- unique_gdd_yld3
Phi_yld3
ordLP_yld3 <- match(nmsu23_nor_gdd_harvest3$GDD, rownames(Phi_yld3))
nmsu23_nor_gdd_harvest3$LPInt_yld3 <- Phi_yld3[ordLP_yld3, "LPInt"]
nmsu23_nor_gdd_harvest3$LPLin_yld3 <- Phi_yld3[ordLP_yld3, "LPLin"]

# Fit RR model (harvest 1)
asreml.options(extra = 200, maxit = 200)

lp_mod_nor_23_yld3 <- { 
  attr(grm_inverse, "INVERSE") <- TRUE
  asreml(
    fixed = GNDVI ~ 1 + at(GDD_fac):Rep,
    random = ~ str(~ Germplasm:LPInt_yld3 + Germplasm:LPLin_yld3, ~ us(2):vm(Germplasm, grm_inverse)) + str(~ Plot:LPInt_yld3 + Plot:LPLin_yld3, ~ us(2):id(Plot)),
    residual = ~ dsum(~ units | GDD_fac),
    data = nmsu23_nor_gdd_harvest3)}

summary(lp_mod_nor_23_yld3)$varcomp
lp_mod_nor_23_yld3 <- update.asreml(lp_mod_nor_23_yld3, start = lp_mod_nor_23_yld3$gammas)

# Save random effects (BLUPs)
blups_yld3 <- lp_mod_nor_23_yld3$coefficients$random
blups_yld3

# --- Convert full BLUPs to a data frame ---
blups_df_yld3 <- as.data.frame(blups_yld3) %>% rename(solution = 1)
blups_df_yld3
# Add term names (simplify)
blups_df_yld3$term <- gsub(":.*", "", rownames(blups_df_yld3))

# --- Filter subsets ---
# BLUP_germplasm_yld3 <- blups_df_yld3 %>% filter(grepl("^Germplasm", rownames(blups_df_yld3)))
BLUP_spa_int_yld3 <- blups_df_yld3 %>% 
  filter(grepl("^Plot_.*LPInt_yld3$", rownames(blups_df_yld3)))

BLUP_spa_slp_yld3 <- blups_df_yld3 %>%

# --- Spatial BLUPs ---
BLUP_spa_int_yld3$solution   # Intercepts

spa_BLUP_matrix_yld3

# ---------- Extract spatial BLUPs as PEE (Permanent Environmental Effects) ----------

# Convert matrix into a data frame for including it in the model below cz my model expects columns in the data frame

# add these as columns in my data file
```

### 2. GEER
 - NOTE: yld#, PEE_###, Check AR model (full or 1D)

```{r GEER between all rep combinations for yld3 Nor 2023, 04282026}
### ---------------------------------------------------------
### 1. Function: Fit model and extract genomic BLUPs
### ---------------------------------------------------------
get_gblup_yld3_nor23 <- function(dat, model_type = c("base", "spa", "pee"), grm_inverse) {
  
  # Ensure GRM is treated as inverse relationship matrix
  attr(grm_inverse, "INVERSE") <- TRUE
  
  # Match model type argument
  model_type <- match.arg(model_type)

  # ---------------------------------------------------------
  # Fit model (robust to failure)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------
  fit <- tryCatch({
    
    if (model_type == "base") {
      # Baseline genomic model (no spatial/environmental correction)
      asreml(
        fixed   = yld3 ~ 1 , # we dont need rep here cz the data is only for one rep
        random  = ~ vm(Germplasm, grm_inverse),
        residual= ~ id(units),
        data    = dat
      )
      
    } else if (model_type == "spa") {
      # Genomic model + 2D autoregressive spatial structure
      asreml(
        fixed   = yld3 ~ 1 , # we dont need rep here cz the data is only for one rep
        random  = ~ vm(Germplasm, grm_inverse) + ar1(Row):ar1(Range),
        residual= ~ id(units),
        data    = dat
      )
      
    } else if (model_type == "pee") {
      # Genomic model + permanent environmental effect (PEE)
      asreml(
        fixed   = yld3 ~ 1 + PEE_181, #!!! PEE
        random  = ~ vm(Germplasm, grm_inverse),
        residual= ~ id(units),
        data    = dat
      )
    }
    
  }, error = function(e) NULL)   # Return NULL if model fails

  # If model fitting failed → skip
  if (is.null(fit)) return(NULL)

  # ---------------------------------------------------------
  # Extract genomic BLUPs (u_a)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------
  blup <- tryCatch(coef(fit)$random, error = function(e) NULL)
  
  # If extraction failed → skip
  if (is.null(blup)) return(NULL)

  # Keep only Germplasm effects
  blup <- blup[grep("Germplasm", rownames(blup)), , drop = FALSE]
  
  # If no genetic effects found → skip
  if (nrow(blup) == 0) return(NULL)

  # Convert to named numeric vector
  out <- blup[, 1]
  names(out) <- rownames(blup)

  return(out)
}


### ---------------------------------------------------------
### 2. Function: Compute GEER across all replicate pairs
### ---------------------------------------------------------
geer_all_pairs_yld3_nor23 <- function(dat, grm_inverse, rep_col = "Rep") {
  
  # Split dataset by replicate
  rep_list <- split(dat, dat[[rep_col]])
  rep_names <- names(rep_list)
  
  # All pairwise replicate combinations
  pairs <- combn(rep_names, 2, simplify = FALSE)

  # Loop over replicate pairs
  res <- lapply(pairs, function(p) {
    
    d1 <- rep_list[[p[1]]]
    d2 <- rep_list[[p[2]]]

    models <- c("base", "spa", "pee")

    # Compute GEER for each model
    pair_res <- lapply(models, function(m) {
      
      g1 <- get_gblup_yld3_nor23(d1, m, grm_inverse)
      g2 <- get_gblup_yld3_nor23(d2, m, grm_inverse)

      # Skip if either replicate failed
      if (is.null(g1) || is.null(g2)) return(NULL)

      # Align common germplasm entries
      common_ids <- intersect(names(g1), names(g2))
      if (length(common_ids) < 2) return(NULL)

      # Compute correlations
      pear <- tryCatch(
        cor(g1[common_ids], g2[common_ids]),
        error = function(e) NA_real_
      )
      
      spear <- tryCatch(
        cor(g1[common_ids], g2[common_ids], method = "spearman"),
        error = function(e) NA_real_
      )

      # Return results
      data.frame(
        Rep1 = p[1],
        Rep2 = p[2],
        Model = m,
        N_common = length(common_ids),
        Pearson = pear,
        Spearman = spear,
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      )
    })

    do.call(rbind, pair_res)
  })

  # Combine all results
  res <- do.call(rbind, res)
  rownames(res) <- NULL

  return(res)
}


### ---------------------------------------------------------
### 3. Run GEER analysis
### ---------------------------------------------------------
GEER_results_yld3_nor23 <- geer_all_pairs_yld3_nor23(
  nmsu23_nor_pheno,
  grm_inverse
)

GEER_results_yld3_nor23


### ---------------------------------------------------------
### 4. Summary statistics
### ---------------------------------------------------------

# Number of valid comparisons per model
table(GEER_results_yld3_nor23$Model)

# Mean GEER per model
aggregate(
  cbind(Pearson, Spearman) ~ Model,
  GEER_results_yld3_nor23,
  mean
)


### ---------------------------------------------------------
### 5. Visualization: GEER (Pearson)
### ---------------------------------------------------------

# Ensure consistent ordering for plotting
GEER_results_yld3_nor23$Model <- factor(
  GEER_results_yld3_nor23$Model,
  levels = c("base", "spa", "pee"),
  labels = c("Base", "Spa(AR)", "PEE"))

# Boxplot of Pearson GEER
boxplot(
  Pearson ~ Model,
  data = GEER_results_yld3_nor23,
  col = c("grey70", "skyblue", "tomato"),
  border = "black",
  ylab = "GEER (Pearson correlation)",
  xlab = "Model",
  main = "Genotypic Effect Estimation across Replicates (GEER)\nHarvest 3, NOR 2023",
  outline = TRUE
)

# Overlay individual replicate-pair estimates
stripchart(
  Pearson ~ Model,
  data = GEER_results_yld3_nor23,
  vertical = TRUE,
  method = "jitter",
  pch = 19,
  col = "black",
  add = TRUE
)
```

```{r yld3, PEE_181 Validity of GEER Resultst, nor23, 06052026}
asreml.options(extra = 200, maxit = 200)

# Rep 1
uni_yld3_spa_rep1 <- asreml(
  fixed = yld3 ~ 1, # per rep, so no need of Rep here
  random = ~ vm(Germplasm, grm_inverse) + ar1(Row):ar1(Range),
  residual = ~ id(units),
  data = nmsu23_nor_pheno %>% filter(Rep == 1))

# Rep 2
uni_yld3_spa_rep2 <- asreml(
  fixed = yld3 ~ 1,
  random = ~ vm(Germplasm, grm_inverse) + ar1(Row):ar1(Range),
  residual = ~ id(units),
  data = nmsu23_nor_pheno %>% filter(Rep == 2))

# Rep 3
uni_yld3_spa_rep3 <- asreml(
  fixed = yld3 ~ 1,
  random = ~ vm(Germplasm, grm_inverse) + ar1(Row):ar1(Range),
  residual = ~ id(units),
  data = nmsu23_nor_pheno %>% filter(Rep == 3))

# Rep 4
uni_yld3_spa_rep4 <- asreml(
  fixed = yld3 ~ 1,
  random = ~ vm(Germplasm, grm_inverse) + ar1(Row):ar1(Range),
  residual = ~ id(units),
  data = nmsu23_nor_pheno %>% filter(Rep == 4))


# ============================================================
# 4. PEE MODEL — FIT PER REP
# ============================================================

# Rep 1
uni_yld3_pee_rep1 <- asreml(
  fixed = yld3 ~ 1 + PEE_181, ### !!!
  random = ~ vm(Germplasm, grm_inverse),
  residual = ~ id(units),
  data = nmsu23_nor_pheno %>% filter(Rep == 1))

# Rep 2
uni_yld3_pee_rep2 <- asreml(
  fixed = yld3 ~ 1 + PEE_181,

  data = nmsu23_nor_pheno %>% filter(Rep == 2))

# Rep 3
uni_yld3_pee_rep3 <- asreml(
  fixed = yld3 ~ 1 + PEE_181,
  random = ~ vm(Germplasm, grm_inverse),
  residual = ~ id(units),
  data = nmsu23_nor_pheno %>% filter(Rep == 3))

# Rep 4

  fixed = yld3 ~ 1 + PEE_181,
  random = ~ vm(Germplasm, grm_inverse),
  residual = ~ id(units),
  data = nmsu23_nor_pheno %>% filter(Rep == 4))


# ============================================================
# 5. EXTRACT GENOTYPE BLUPS (DIRECT: FIRST 22 values are gblups)
# ============================================================

# ---- Base model ----
gblups_base_all_reps_yld3 <- uni_nmsu23_nor_yld3$coefficients$random[1:22]
gblups_base_all_reps_yld3

# ---- base per rep model ----
gblups_base_rep1_yld3 <- uni_yld3_base_rep1$coefficients$random[1:22]
gblups_base_rep2_yld3 <- uni_yld3_base_rep2$coefficients$random[1:22]
gblups_base_rep3_yld3 <- uni_yld3_base_rep3$coefficients$random[1:22]
gblups_base_rep4_yld3 <- uni_yld3_base_rep4$coefficients$random[1:22]

gblups_spa_rep2_yld3 <- uni_yld3_spa_rep2$coefficients$random[1:22]
gblups_spa_rep3_yld3 <- uni_yld3_spa_rep3$coefficients$random[1:22]
gblups_spa_rep4_yld3 <- uni_yld3_spa_rep4$coefficients$random[1:22]

# ---- PEE model ----

gblups_pee_rep2_yld3 <- uni_yld3_pee_rep2$coefficients$random[1:22]

gblups_pee_rep4_yld3 <- uni_yld3_pee_rep4$coefficients$random[1:22]

# ============================================================
# 4. Correlation
```

###  Spatially Corrected Rep-wise Yield Correlation (SCRYC)
 - correlation of phenotypes/yield after removing spatial effects across reps
- PEE much better cz autoreg.is not capturing
```{r  Spatially Corrected Yiled, yld3, 04282026}
# ============================================================
# NEW METRIC: SPATIALLY CORRECTED YIELD (yld3_nor23)
# ============================================================

# -------------------------------
# 1. PREPARE WORKING DATA
# -------------------------------
nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC <- nmsu23_nor_pheno

# ============================================================
# 1.1 SPATIAL (AR1): EXTRACT + ALIGN SPATIAL BLUPS
# ============================================================

# Extract all random effects
spa_blup_yld3_nor23 <- uni_nmsu23_nor_yld3_spa$coefficients$random
spa_blup_yld3_nor23
# Extract ONLY Row:Range spatial effects (correct pattern)
spa_eff_yld3_nor23 <- spa_blup_yld3_nor23[
  grep("^Row_[0-9]+:Range_[0-9]+", rownames(spa_blup_yld3_nor23)),
  , drop = FALSE]
spa_eff_yld3_nor23

# Build lookup table (use column name "effect")
spa_df_yld3_nor23 <- data.frame(
  RowRange = rownames(spa_eff_yld3_nor23),
  spa_eff_yld3_nor23 = spa_eff_yld3_nor23[,"effect"],
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
spa_df_yld3_nor23
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Create matching key in phenotype data
# ------------------------------------------------------------
nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$RowRange <- paste0(
  "Row_", nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$Row,
  ":Range_", nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$Range)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Match WITHOUT reordering (IMPORTANT)
# ------------------------------------------------------------

match_idx <- match(
  nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$RowRange,
  spa_df_yld3_nor23$RowRange)

nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$spa_eff_yld3_nor23 <- 
  spa_df_yld3_nor23$spa_eff_yld3_nor23[match_idx]
 # i doubled check the spatial blups and these columns to make sure i am getting what i wanted

# Sanity check (must be zero)
sum(is.na(nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$spa_eff_yld3_nor23)) # 0

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Corrected yield (AR1)
# ------------------------------------------------------------

nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$yld3_spa_corr_nor23 <- 
  nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$yld3 - nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$spa_eff_yld3_nor23




# ============================================================
# 1.2 PEE: DIRECT SPATIAL CORRECTION
# ============================================================

 # we need to scale PEE to be able to use it for spatial correction

# lets see
# Extract coefficient
beta_pee_yld3_nor23 <- uni_nmsu23_nor_yld3_pee$coefficients$fixed["PEE_181", "effect"]
beta_pee_yld3_nor23   #  

# Apply correct spatial correction
nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$yld3_pee_corr_nor23 <- 
  nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$yld3 - 
  beta_pee_yld3_nor23 * nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$PEE_181


# ============================================================
# 2. REP-WISE CORRELATIONS
# ============================================================

# -------------------------------
# SPLIT DATA BY REP
# -------------------------------

rep1_yld3_nor23 <- nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC[nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$Rep == 1, ]
dim(nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC) # 144*76
dim(rep1_yld3_nor23) # should be 144/4 = 36 and it is. JUST SANITY CHECK
rep2_yld3_nor23 <- nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC[nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$Rep == 2, ]
rep3_yld3_nor23 <- nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC[nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$Rep == 3, ]
rep4_yld3_nor23 <- nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC[nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$Rep == 4, ]

# Align by genotype
rep1_yld3_nor23 <- rep1_yld3_nor23[order(rep1_yld3_nor23$Germplasm), ]
rep2_yld3_nor23 <- rep2_yld3_nor23[order(rep2_yld3_nor23$Germplasm), ]
rep3_yld3_nor23 <- rep3_yld3_nor23[order(rep3_yld3_nor23$Germplasm), ]
rep4_yld3_nor23 <- rep4_yld3_nor23[order(rep4_yld3_nor23$Germplasm), ]


# ============================================================
# 1. RAW YIELD
# ============================================================

cor_raw_yld3_nor23 <- c(
  cor(rep1_yld3_nor23$yld3, rep2_yld3_nor23$yld3, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep1_yld3_nor23$yld3, rep3_yld3_nor23$yld3, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep1_yld3_nor23$yld3, rep4_yld3_nor23$yld3, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep2_yld3_nor23$yld3, rep3_yld3_nor23$yld3, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep2_yld3_nor23$yld3, rep4_yld3_nor23$yld3, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep3_yld3_nor23$yld3, rep4_yld3_nor23$yld3, use="complete.obs") )

df_raw_yld3_nor23 <- data.frame(
  Model = "Raw",
  Correlation = cor_raw_yld3_nor23)
df_raw_yld3_nor23

# ============================================================
# 2. AR1 CORRECTED
# ============================================================

cor_spa_cor_yld3_nor23 <- c(
  cor(rep1_yld3_nor23$yld3_spa_corr_nor23, rep2_yld3_nor23$yld3_spa_corr_nor23, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep1_yld3_nor23$yld3_spa_corr_nor23, rep3_yld3_nor23$yld3_spa_corr_nor23, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep1_yld3_nor23$yld3_spa_corr_nor23, rep4_yld3_nor23$yld3_spa_corr_nor23, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep2_yld3_nor23$yld3_spa_corr_nor23, rep3_yld3_nor23$yld3_spa_corr_nor23, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep2_yld3_nor23$yld3_spa_corr_nor23, rep4_yld3_nor23$yld3_spa_corr_nor23, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep3_yld3_nor23$yld3_spa_corr_nor23, rep4_yld3_nor23$yld3_spa_corr_nor23, use="complete.obs"))

df_spa_yld3_nor23 <- data.frame(
  Model = "Spa(AR1)",
  Correlation = cor_spa_cor_yld3_nor23)
df_spa_yld3_nor23

# ============================================================
# 3. PEE CORRECTED
# ============================================================

cor_pee_cor_yld3_nor23 <- c(
  cor(rep1_yld3_nor23$yld3_pee_corr_nor23, rep2_yld3_nor23$yld3_pee_corr_nor23, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep1_yld3_nor23$yld3_pee_corr_nor23, rep3_yld3_nor23$yld3_pee_corr_nor23, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep1_yld3_nor23$yld3_pee_corr_nor23, rep4_yld3_nor23$yld3_pee_corr_nor23, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep2_yld3_nor23$yld3_pee_corr_nor23, rep3_yld3_nor23$yld3_pee_corr_nor23, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep2_yld3_nor23$yld3_pee_corr_nor23, rep4_yld3_nor23$yld3_pee_corr_nor23, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep3_yld3_nor23$yld3_pee_corr_nor23, rep4_yld3_nor23$yld3_pee_corr_nor23, use="complete.obs"))

df_pee_yld3_nor23 <- data.frame(
  Model = "PEE",
  Correlation = cor_pee_cor_yld3_nor23)
df_pee_yld3_nor23

# ============================================================
# 4. COMBINE + PLOT
# ============================================================

df_all_yld3_nor23 <- rbind(
  df_raw_yld3_nor23,
  df_spa_yld3_nor23,
  df_pee_yld3_nor23)

df_all_yld3_nor23$Model <- factor(
  df_all_yld3_nor23$Model,
  levels = c("Raw", "Spa(AR1)", "PEE"))

boxplot(
  Correlation ~ Model,
  data = df_all_yld3_nor23,
  col = c("lightgray", "lightblue", "lightgreen"),
  ylab = "Rep-to-rep correlation",
  main = "nor23 yld3: Spatial Correction Comparison",
  ylim = c(0,1)
)

# Summary
aggregate(Correlation ~ Model, df_all_yld3_nor23, mean)
aggregate(Correlation ~ Model, df_all_yld3_nor23, sd)
```

```{r Combined chunk for harvest4 using Random Regression 04282026}
# ---------- PART 0: Manange data file -----------

#  Manage data file: First, assign harvest based on GDD
# first make harvest4 only data file
nmsu23_nor_pheno_gndvi_only_long_harvestwise <- 
  nmsu23_nor_pheno_gndvi_only_long %>%
  mutate(Harvest = case_when(
    # no harvest 1 in this treatment
    GDD >= 119 & GDD <= 153 ~ "Harvest2", # here upper limit is of actual yld
    GDD >= 153 & GDD <= 181 ~ "Harvest3",
    GDD >= 181 & GDD <= 207 ~ "Harvest4",
    GDD >= 207 & GDD <= 243 ~ "Harvest5",
    GDD >= 243 & GDD <= 279 ~ "Harvest6",
    GDD >= 279 & GDD <= 310 ~ "Harvest7"
  ))

# Subset harvest4
nmsu23_nor_gdd_harvest4 <- nmsu23_nor_pheno_gndvi_only_long_harvestwise %>%
  filter(Harvest == "Harvest4") # !!! capital H

# create factor + numeric GDD
nmsu23_nor_gdd_harvest4$GDD_fac <- as.factor(nmsu23_nor_gdd_harvest4$GDD)
nmsu23_nor_gdd_harvest4 <- nmsu23_nor_gdd_harvest4[order(nmsu23_nor_gdd_harvest4$GDD_fac),]

unique(nmsu23_nor_gdd_harvest4$GDD_fac) # 187 192 201 206 207(for yld4)

# Build Legendre basis
unique_gdd_yld4 <- sort(unique(nmsu23_nor_gdd_harvest4$GDD))
unique_gdd_yld4 <- as.numeric(unique_gdd_yld4)

 ######## fitting linear equation
M_yld4 <- stdtime(unique_gdd_yld4, 1) # for linear, 1
lambda_yld4 <- Legendre(1, gengler=TRUE) # for linear, 1 (intercept + slope)

Phi_yld4 <- M_yld4 %*% t(lambda_yld4)
colnames(Phi_yld4) <- c("LPInt", "LPLin")
rownames(Phi_yld4) <- unique_gdd_yld4
Phi_yld4
ordLP_yld4 <- match(nmsu23_nor_gdd_harvest4$GDD, rownames(Phi_yld4))
nmsu23_nor_gdd_harvest4$LPInt_yld4 <- Phi_yld4[ordLP_yld4, "LPInt"]
nmsu23_nor_gdd_harvest4$LPLin_yld4 <- Phi_yld4[ordLP_yld4, "LPLin"]

# Fit RR model (harvest 1)
asreml.options(extra = 200, maxit = 200)

lp_mod_nor_23_yld4 <- { 
  attr(grm_inverse, "INVERSE") <- TRUE
  asreml(
    fixed = GNDVI ~ 1 + at(GDD_fac):Rep,
    random = ~ str(~ Germplasm:LPInt_yld4 + Germplasm:LPLin_yld4, ~ us(2):vm(Germplasm, grm_inverse)) + str(~ Plot:LPInt_yld4 + Plot:LPLin_yld4, ~ us(2):id(Plot)),
    residual = ~ id(units), # for using residuals as independent for each flight : = ~ id(units) # typically use nested structure: dsum(~ units | GDD_fac)
    data = nmsu23_nor_gdd_harvest4)}

summary(lp_mod_nor_23_yld4)$varcomp
lp_mod_nor_23_yld4 <- update.asreml(lp_mod_nor_23_yld4, start = lp_mod_nor_23_yld4$gammas)

# Save random effects (BLUPs)
blups_yld4 <- lp_mod_nor_23_yld4$coefficients$random
blups_yld4

# --- Convert full BLUPs to a data frame ---
blups_df_yld4 <- as.data.frame(blups_yld4) %>% rename(solution = 1)
blups_df_yld4
# Add term names (simplify)
blups_df_yld4$term <- gsub(":.*", "", rownames(blups_df_yld4))

# --- Filter subsets ---
# BLUP_germplasm_yld4 <- blups_df_yld4 %>% filter(grepl("^Germplasm", rownames(blups_df_yld4)))
BLUP_spa_int_yld4 <- blups_df_yld4 %>% 
  filter(grepl("^Plot_.*LPInt_yld4$", rownames(blups_df_yld4)))

BLUP_spa_slp_yld4 <- blups_df_yld4 %>% 
  filter(grepl("^Plot_.*LPLin_yld4$", rownames(blups_df_yld4)))

# --- Spatial BLUPs ---
BLUP_spa_int_yld4$solution   # Intercepts
BLUP_spa_slp_yld4$solution   # Slopes

# --- Combine intercept and slope into a matrix ---
spa_BLUP_matrix_yld4 <- cbind(
  BLUP_spa_int_yld4$solution, 
  BLUP_spa_slp_yld4$solution)
spa_BLUP_matrix_yld4

# ---------- Extract spatial BLUPs as PEE (Permanent Environmental Effects) ----------

# Convert matrix into a data frame for including it in the model below cz my model expects columns in the data frame
nmsu23_nor_spa_yld4 <- as.data.frame(spa_BLUP_matrix_yld4)
# add these as columns in my data file
nmsu23_nor_pheno$spa_int_yld4 <- nmsu23_nor_spa_yld4[,1]
nmsu23_nor_pheno$spa_slp_yld4 <- nmsu23_nor_spa_yld4[,2]

# !!!!!!!!!!!!!!! Permanent Environmental Effect !!!!!!!!!!!!! 
Phi_yld4
# here intercept and slope for GDD on PEE_207 are 1 and 1.7320508 
nmsu23_nor_pheno$PEE_207 <- 
  1 * nmsu23_nor_pheno$spa_int_yld4 +
  1.7320508 * nmsu23_nor_pheno$spa_slp_yld4


# ---------- Step 2: Fit PEE's as fixed regressor on a yield model with spatial correction ----------

# Fit single-trait model for yield (yld4)
# Spatial effects are included as fixed covariates (PEE correction)
uni_nmsu23_nor_yld4_pee <- { 
  attr(grm_inverse, "INVERSE") <- TRUE
  asreml(
    fixed   = yld4 ~ 1 + Rep + PEE_207,   # PEE as fixed regressors !!!!!!!!!!!! check PEE used
    random  = ~ vm(Germplasm, grm_inverse),         # genomic effect
    residual= ~ id(units),
    data    = nmsu23_nor_pheno)}


# Extract variance components
summary(uni_nmsu23_nor_yld4_pee)$varcomp




# 1st model: yield alone genetic model without spatial (autoregressive)
uni_nmsu23_nor_yld4 <- { 
    attr(grm_inverse, "INVERSE") <- TRUE
  asreml(fixed = yld4 ~ 1 + Rep, #rep effect as fixed
         random = ~ vm(Germplasm, grm_inverse),
         residual = ~ id(units),
         data = nmsu23_nor_pheno)}
summary(uni_nmsu23_nor_yld4)$varcomp



# 2nd model: yield alone genetic model with spatial (autoregressive)
## Univariate with autoregressive spatial correction
asreml.options(extra = 200, maxit = 200)

uni_nmsu23_nor_yld4_spa <- {

  asreml(fixed = yld4 ~ 1 + Rep, #rep effect as fixed

summary(uni_nmsu23_nor_yld4_spa)$varcomp


# compare

summary(uni_nmsu23_nor_yld4)$varcomp
summary(uni_nmsu23_nor_yld4_spa)$varcomp
summary(uni_nmsu23_nor_yld4_pee)$varcomp

# heritability

h2_no_spa # 0.23

h2_AR1 # 0.52

h2_PEE # 0.67

 ## just PEE
```

### 2. GEER
 - NOTE: yld#, PEE_###, Check AR model (full or 1D)

```{r GEER between all rep combinations for yld4 Nor 2023, 04282026}
### ---------------------------------------------------------
### 1. Function: Fit model and extract genomic BLUPs
### ---------------------------------------------------------
get_gblup_yld4_nor23 <- function(dat, model_type = c("base", "spa", "pee"), grm_inverse) {
  
  # Ensure GRM is treated as inverse relationship matrix
  attr(grm_inverse, "INVERSE") <- TRUE
  
  # Match model type argument
  model_type <- match.arg(model_type)

  # ---------------------------------------------------------
  # Fit model (robust to failure)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------
  fit <- tryCatch({
    
    if (model_type == "base") {
      # Baseline genomic model (no spatial/environmental correction)
      asreml(
        fixed   = yld4 ~ 1 , # we dont need rep here cz the data is only for one rep
        random  = ~ vm(Germplasm, grm_inverse),
        residual= ~ id(units),
        data    = dat
      )
      
    } else if (model_type == "spa") {
      # Genomic model + 2D autoregressive spatial structure
      asreml(
        fixed   = yld4 ~ 1 , # we dont need rep here cz the data is only for one rep
        random  = ~ vm(Germplasm, grm_inverse) + ar1(Row), # :ar1(Range)
        residual= ~ id(units),
        data    = dat
      )
      
    } else if (model_type == "pee") {
      # Genomic model + permanent environmental effect (PEE)
      asreml(
        fixed   = yld4 ~ 1 + PEE_207, #!!! PEE
        random  = ~ vm(Germplasm, grm_inverse),
        residual= ~ id(units),
        data    = dat
      )
    }
    
  }, error = function(e) NULL)   # Return NULL if model fails

  # If model fitting failed → skip
  if (is.null(fit)) return(NULL)

  # ---------------------------------------------------------
  # Extract genomic BLUPs (u_a)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------
  blup <- tryCatch(coef(fit)$random, error = function(e) NULL)
  
  # If extraction failed → skip
  if (is.null(blup)) return(NULL)

  # Keep only Germplasm effects
  blup <- blup[grep("Germplasm", rownames(blup)), , drop = FALSE]
  
  # If no genetic effects found → skip
  if (nrow(blup) == 0) return(NULL)

  # Convert to named numeric vector
  out <- blup[, 1]
  names(out) <- rownames(blup)

  return(out)
}


### ---------------------------------------------------------
### 2. Function: Compute GEER across all replicate pairs
### ---------------------------------------------------------
geer_all_pairs_yld4_nor23 <- function(dat, grm_inverse, rep_col = "Rep") {
  
  # Split dataset by replicate
  rep_list <- split(dat, dat[[rep_col]])
  rep_names <- names(rep_list)
  
  # All pairwise replicate combinations
  pairs <- combn(rep_names, 2, simplify = FALSE)

  # Loop over replicate pairs
  res <- lapply(pairs, function(p) {
    
    d1 <- rep_list[[p[1]]]
    d2 <- rep_list[[p[2]]]

    models <- c("base", "spa", "pee")

    # Compute GEER for each model
    pair_res <- lapply(models, function(m) {
      
      g1 <- get_gblup_yld4_nor23(d1, m, grm_inverse)
      g2 <- get_gblup_yld4_nor23(d2, m, grm_inverse)

      # Skip if either replicate failed
      if (is.null(g1) || is.null(g2)) return(NULL)

      # Align common germplasm entries
      common_ids <- intersect(names(g1), names(g2))
      if (length(common_ids) < 2) return(NULL)

      # Compute correlations
      pear <- tryCatch(
        cor(g1[common_ids], g2[common_ids]),
        error = function(e) NA_real_
      )
      
      spear <- tryCatch(
        cor(g1[common_ids], g2[common_ids], method = "spearman"),
        error = function(e) NA_real_
      )

      # Return results
      data.frame(
        Rep1 = p[1],
        Rep2 = p[2],
        Model = m,
        N_common = length(common_ids),
        Pearson = pear,
        Spearman = spear,
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      )
    })

    do.call(rbind, pair_res)
  })

  # Combine all results
  res <- do.call(rbind, res)
  rownames(res) <- NULL

  return(res)
}


### ---------------------------------------------------------
### 3. Run GEER analysis
### ---------------------------------------------------------
GEER_results_yld4_nor23 <- geer_all_pairs_yld4_nor23(
  nmsu23_nor_pheno,
  grm_inverse
)

GEER_results_yld4_nor23


### ---------------------------------------------------------
### 4. Summary statistics
### ---------------------------------------------------------

# Number of valid comparisons per model
table(GEER_results_yld4_nor23$Model)

# Mean GEER per model
aggregate(
  cbind(Pearson, Spearman) ~ Model,
  GEER_results_yld4_nor23,
  mean
)


### ---------------------------------------------------------
### 5. Visualization: GEER (Pearson)
### ---------------------------------------------------------

# Ensure consistent ordering for plotting
GEER_results_yld4_nor23$Model <- factor(
  GEER_results_yld4_nor23$Model,
  levels = c("base", "spa", "pee"),
  labels = c("Base", "Spa(AR)", "PEE"))

# Boxplot of Pearson GEER
boxplot(
  Pearson ~ Model,
  data = GEER_results_yld4_nor23,
  col = c("grey70", "skyblue", "tomato"),
  border = "black",
  ylab = "GEER (Pearson correlation)",
  xlab = "Model",
  main = "Genotypic Effect Estimation across Replicates (GEER)\nHarvest 4, NOR 2023",
  outline = TRUE
)

# Overlay individual replicate-pair estimates
stripchart(
  Pearson ~ Model,
  data = GEER_results_yld4_nor23,
  vertical = TRUE,
  method = "jitter",
  pch = 19,
  col = "black",
  add = TRUE
)
```

###  Spatially Corrected Rep-wise Yield Correlation (SCRYC)
 - correlation of phenotypes/yield after removing spatial effects across reps
- PEE much better cz autoreg.is not capturing
```{r  Spatially Corrected Yiled, yld4, 04282026}
# ============================================================
# NEW METRIC: SPATIALLY CORRECTED YIELD (yld4_nor23)
# ============================================================

# -------------------------------
# 1. PREPARE WORKING DATA
# -------------------------------
nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC <- nmsu23_nor_pheno

# ============================================================
# 1.1 SPATIAL (AR1): EXTRACT + ALIGN SPATIAL BLUPS
# ============================================================

# Extract all random effects
spa_blup_yld4_nor23 <- uni_nmsu23_nor_yld4_spa$coefficients$random
spa_blup_yld4_nor23
# Extract ONLY Row:Range spatial effects (correct pattern)
spa_eff_yld4_nor23 <- spa_blup_yld4_nor23[
  grep("^Row_[0-9]+:Range_[0-9]+", rownames(spa_blup_yld4_nor23)),
  , drop = FALSE]
spa_eff_yld4_nor23

# Build lookup table (use column name "effect")
spa_df_yld4_nor23 <- data.frame(
  RowRange = rownames(spa_eff_yld4_nor23),
  spa_eff_yld4_nor23 = spa_eff_yld4_nor23[,"effect"],
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
spa_df_yld4_nor23
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Create matching key in phenotype data
# ------------------------------------------------------------
nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$RowRange <- paste0(
  "Row_", nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$Row,
  ":Range_", nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$Range)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Match WITHOUT reordering (IMPORTANT)
# ------------------------------------------------------------

match_idx <- match(
  nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$RowRange,
  spa_df_yld4_nor23$RowRange)

nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$spa_eff_yld4_nor23 <- 
  spa_df_yld4_nor23$spa_eff_yld4_nor23[match_idx]
 # i doubled check the spatial blups and these columns to make sure i am getting what i wanted

# Sanity check (must be zero)
sum(is.na(nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$spa_eff_yld4_nor23)) # 0

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Corrected yield (AR1)
# ------------------------------------------------------------

nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$yld4_spa_corr_nor23 <- 
  nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$yld4 - nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$spa_eff_yld4_nor23




# ============================================================
# 1.2 PEE: DIRECT SPATIAL CORRECTION
# ============================================================

 # we need to scale PEE to be able to use it for spatial correction

# lets see
# Extract coefficient
beta_pee_yld4_nor23 <- uni_nmsu23_nor_yld4_pee$coefficients$fixed["PEE_207", "effect"]
beta_pee_yld4_nor23   #  

# Apply correct spatial correction
nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$yld4_pee_corr_nor23 <- 
  nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$yld4 - 
  beta_pee_yld4_nor23 * nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$PEE_207


# ============================================================
# 2. REP-WISE CORRELATIONS
# ============================================================

# -------------------------------
# SPLIT DATA BY REP
# -------------------------------

rep1_yld4_nor23 <- nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC[nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$Rep == 1, ]
```

### 2. GEER
 - NOTE: yld#, PEE_###, Check AR model (full or 1D)

```{r GEER between all rep combinations for yld5 Nor 2023, 04282026}
### ---------------------------------------------------------
### 1. Function: Fit model and extract genomic BLUPs
### ---------------------------------------------------------
get_gblup_yld5_nor23 <- function(dat, model_type = c("base", "spa", "pee"), grm_inverse) {
  
  # Ensure GRM is treated as inverse relationship matrix
  attr(grm_inverse, "INVERSE") <- TRUE
  
  # Match model type argument
  model_type <- match.arg(model_type)

  # ---------------------------------------------------------
  # Fit model (robust to failure)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------
  fit <- tryCatch({
    
    if (model_type == "base") {
      # Baseline genomic model (no spatial/environmental correction)
      asreml(
        fixed   = yld5 ~ 1 , # we dont need rep here cz the data is only for one rep
        random  = ~ vm(Germplasm, grm_inverse),
        residual= ~ id(units),
        data    = dat
      )
      
    } else if (model_type == "spa") {
      # Genomic model + 2D autoregressive spatial structure
      asreml(
        fixed   = yld5 ~ 1 , # we dont need rep here cz the data is only for one rep
        random  = ~ vm(Germplasm, grm_inverse) + ar1(Row):ar1(Range),
        residual= ~ id(units),
        data    = dat
      )
      
    } else if (model_type == "pee") {
      # Genomic model + permanent environmental effect (PEE)
      asreml(
        fixed   = yld5 ~ 1 + PEE_243, #!!! PEE
        random  = ~ vm(Germplasm, grm_inverse),
        residual= ~ id(units),
        data    = dat
      )
    }
    
  }, error = function(e) NULL)   # Return NULL if model fails

  # If model fitting failed → skip
  if (is.null(fit)) return(NULL)

  # ---------------------------------------------------------
  # Extract genomic BLUPs (u_a)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------
  blup <- tryCatch(coef(fit)$random, error = function(e) NULL)
  
  # If extraction failed → skip
  if (is.null(blup)) return(NULL)

  # Keep only Germplasm effects
  blup <- blup[grep("Germplasm", rownames(blup)), , drop = FALSE]
  
  # If no genetic effects found → skip
  if (nrow(blup) == 0) return(NULL)

  # Convert to named numeric vector
  out <- blup[, 1]
  names(out) <- rownames(blup)

  return(out)
}


### ---------------------------------------------------------
### 2. Function: Compute GEER across all replicate pairs
### ---------------------------------------------------------
geer_all_pairs_yld5_nor23 <- function(dat, grm_inverse, rep_col = "Rep") {
  
  # Split dataset by replicate
  rep_list <- split(dat, dat[[rep_col]])
  rep_names <- names(rep_list)
  
  # All pairwise replicate combinations
  pairs <- combn(rep_names, 2, simplify = FALSE)

  # Loop over replicate pairs
  res <- lapply(pairs, function(p) {
    
    d1 <- rep_list[[p[1]]]
    d2 <- rep_list[[p[2]]]

    models <- c("base", "spa", "pee")

    # Compute GEER for each model
    pair_res <- lapply(models, function(m) {
      
      g1 <- get_gblup_yld5_nor23(d1, m, grm_inverse)
      g2 <- get_gblup_yld5_nor23(d2, m, grm_inverse)

      # Skip if either replicate failed
      if (is.null(g1) || is.null(g2)) return(NULL)

      # Align common germplasm entries
      common_ids <- intersect(names(g1), names(g2))
      if (length(common_ids) < 2) return(NULL)

      # Compute correlations
      pear <- tryCatch(
        cor(g1[common_ids], g2[common_ids]),
        error = function(e) NA_real_
      )
      
      spear <- tryCatch(
        cor(g1[common_ids], g2[common_ids], method = "spearman"),
        error = function(e) NA_real_
      )

      # Return results
      data.frame(
        Rep1 = p[1],
        Rep2 = p[2],
        Model = m,
        N_common = length(common_ids),
        Pearson = pear,
        Spearman = spear,
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      )
    })

    do.call(rbind, pair_res)
  })

  # Combine all results
  res <- do.call(rbind, res)
  rownames(res) <- NULL

  return(res)
}


### ---------------------------------------------------------
### 3. Run GEER analysis
### ---------------------------------------------------------
GEER_results_yld5_nor23 <- geer_all_pairs_yld5_nor23(
  nmsu23_nor_pheno,
  grm_inverse
)

GEER_results_yld5_nor23


### ---------------------------------------------------------
### 4. Summary statistics
### ---------------------------------------------------------

# Number of valid comparisons per model
table(GEER_results_yld5_nor23$Model)

# Mean GEER per model
aggregate(
  cbind(Pearson, Spearman) ~ Model,
  GEER_results_yld5_nor23,
  mean
)


### ---------------------------------------------------------
### 5. Visualization: GEER (Pearson)
### ---------------------------------------------------------

# Ensure consistent ordering for plotting
GEER_results_yld5_nor23$Model <- factor(
  GEER_results_yld5_nor23$Model,
  levels = c("base", "spa", "pee"),
  labels = c("Base", "Spa(AR)", "PEE"))

# Boxplot of Pearson GEER
boxplot(
  Pearson ~ Model,
  data = GEER_results_yld5_nor23,
  col = c("grey70", "skyblue", "tomato"),
  border = "black",
  ylab = "GEER (Pearson correlation)",
  xlab = "Model",
  main = "Genotypic Effect Estimation across Replicates (GEER)\nHarvest 5, NOR 2023",
  outline = TRUE
)

# Overlay individual replicate-pair estimates
stripchart(
  Pearson ~ Model,
  data = GEER_results_yld5_nor23,
  vertical = TRUE,
  method = "jitter",
  pch = 19,
  col = "black",
  add = TRUE
)
```

###  Spatially Corrected Rep-wise Yield Correlation (SCRYC)
 - correlation of phenotypes/yield after removing spatial effects across reps
- PEE much better cz autoreg.is not capturing
```{r  Spatially Corrected Yiled, yld5, 04282026}
# ============================================================
# NEW METRIC: SPATIALLY CORRECTED YIELD (yld5_nor23)
# ============================================================

# -------------------------------
# 1. PREPARE WORKING DATA
# -------------------------------
nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC <- nmsu23_nor_pheno

# ============================================================
# 1.1 SPATIAL (AR1): EXTRACT + ALIGN SPATIAL BLUPS
# ============================================================

# Extract all random effects
spa_blup_yld5_nor23 <- uni_nmsu23_nor_yld5_spa$coefficients$random
spa_blup_yld5_nor23
# Extract ONLY Row:Range spatial effects (correct pattern)
spa_eff_yld5_nor23 <- spa_blup_yld5_nor23[
  grep("^Row_[0-9]+:Range_[0-9]+", rownames(spa_blup_yld5_nor23)),
  , drop = FALSE]
spa_eff_yld5_nor23

# Build lookup table (use column name "effect")
spa_df_yld5_nor23 <- data.frame(
  RowRange = rownames(spa_eff_yld5_nor23),
  spa_eff_yld5_nor23 = spa_eff_yld5_nor23[,"effect"],
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
spa_df_yld5_nor23
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Create matching key in phenotype data
# ------------------------------------------------------------
nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$RowRange <- paste0(
  "Row_", nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$Row,
  ":Range_", nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$Range)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Match WITHOUT reordering (IMPORTANT)
# ------------------------------------------------------------

match_idx <- match(
  nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$RowRange,
  spa_df_yld5_nor23$RowRange)

nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$spa_eff_yld5_nor23 <- 
  spa_df_yld5_nor23$spa_eff_yld5_nor23[match_idx]
 # i doubled check the spatial blups and these columns to make sure i am getting what i wanted

# Sanity check (must be zero)
sum(is.na(nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$spa_eff_yld5_nor23)) # 0

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Corrected yield (AR1)
# ------------------------------------------------------------

nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$yld5_spa_corr_nor23 <- 
  nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$yld5 - nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$spa_eff_yld5_nor23




# ============================================================
# 1.2 PEE: DIRECT SPATIAL CORRECTION
# ============================================================

 # we need to scale PEE to be able to use it for spatial correction

# lets see
# Extract coefficient
beta_pee_yld5_nor23 <- uni_nmsu23_nor_yld5_pee$coefficients$fixed["PEE_243", "effect"]
beta_pee_yld5_nor23   #  

# Apply correct spatial correction
nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$yld5_pee_corr_nor23 <- 
  nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$yld5 - 
  beta_pee_yld5_nor23 * nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$PEE_243


# ============================================================
# 2. REP-WISE CORRELATIONS
# ============================================================

# -------------------------------
# SPLIT DATA BY REP
# -------------------------------

rep1_yld5_nor23 <- nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC[nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$Rep == 1, ]
dim(nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC) # 144*82
dim(rep1_yld5_nor23) # should be 144/4 = 36 and it is. JUST SANITY CHECK
rep2_yld5_nor23 <- nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC[nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$Rep == 2, ]
rep3_yld5_nor23 <- nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC[nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$Rep == 3, ]
rep4_yld5_nor23 <- nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC[nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$Rep == 4, ]

# Align by genotype
rep1_yld5_nor23 <- rep1_yld5_nor23[order(rep1_yld5_nor23$Germplasm), ]
rep2_yld5_nor23 <- rep2_yld5_nor23[order(rep2_yld5_nor23$Germplasm), ]
rep3_yld5_nor23 <- rep3_yld5_nor23[order(rep3_yld5_nor23$Germplasm), ]
rep4_yld5_nor23 <- rep4_yld5_nor23[order(rep4_yld5_nor23$Germplasm), ]


# ============================================================
# 1. RAW YIELD
# ============================================================

cor_raw_yld5_nor23 <- c(
  cor(rep1_yld5_nor23$yld5, rep2_yld5_nor23$yld5, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep1_yld5_nor23$yld5, rep3_yld5_nor23$yld5, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep1_yld5_nor23$yld5, rep4_yld5_nor23$yld5, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep2_yld5_nor23$yld5, rep3_yld5_nor23$yld5, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep2_yld5_nor23$yld5, rep4_yld5_nor23$yld5, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep3_yld5_nor23$yld5, rep4_yld5_nor23$yld5, use="complete.obs") )

df_raw_yld5_nor23 <- data.frame(
  Model = "Raw",
  Correlation = cor_raw_yld5_nor23)
df_raw_yld5_nor23

# ============================================================
# 2. AR1 CORRECTED
# ============================================================

cor_spa_cor_yld5_nor23 <- c(
  cor(rep1_yld5_nor23$yld5_spa_corr_nor23, rep2_yld5_nor23$yld5_spa_corr_nor23, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep1_yld5_nor23$yld5_spa_corr_nor23, rep3_yld5_nor23$yld5_spa_corr_nor23, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep1_yld5_nor23$yld5_spa_corr_nor23, rep4_yld5_nor23$yld5_spa_corr_nor23, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep2_yld5_nor23$yld5_spa_corr_nor23, rep3_yld5_nor23$yld5_spa_corr_nor23, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep2_yld5_nor23$yld5_spa_corr_nor23, rep4_yld5_nor23$yld5_spa_corr_nor23, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep3_yld5_nor23$yld5_spa_corr_nor23, rep4_yld5_nor23$yld5_spa_corr_nor23, use="complete.obs"))

df_spa_yld5_nor23 <- data.frame(
  Model = "Spa(AR1)",
  Correlation = cor_spa_cor_yld5_nor23)
df_spa_yld5_nor23

# ============================================================
# 3. PEE CORRECTED
# ============================================================

cor_pee_cor_yld5_nor23 <- c(
  cor(rep1_yld5_nor23$yld5_pee_corr_nor23, rep2_yld5_nor23$yld5_pee_corr_nor23, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep1_yld5_nor23$yld5_pee_corr_nor23, rep3_yld5_nor23$yld5_pee_corr_nor23, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep1_yld5_nor23$yld5_pee_corr_nor23, rep4_yld5_nor23$yld5_pee_corr_nor23, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep2_yld5_nor23$yld5_pee_corr_nor23, rep3_yld5_nor23$yld5_pee_corr_nor23, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep2_yld5_nor23$yld5_pee_corr_nor23, rep4_yld5_nor23$yld5_pee_corr_nor23, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep3_yld5_nor23$yld5_pee_corr_nor23, rep4_yld5_nor23$yld5_pee_corr_nor23, use="complete.obs"))

df_pee_yld5_nor23 <- data.frame(
  Model = "PEE",
  Correlation = cor_pee_cor_yld5_nor23)
df_pee_yld5_nor23

# ============================================================
# 4. COMBINE + PLOT
# ============================================================

df_all_yld5_nor23 <- rbind(
  df_raw_yld5_nor23,
  df_spa_yld5_nor23,
  df_pee_yld5_nor23)

df_all_yld5_nor23$Model <- factor(
  df_all_yld5_nor23$Model,
  levels = c("Raw", "Spa(AR1)", "PEE"))

boxplot(
  Correlation ~ Model,
  data = df_all_yld5_nor23,
  col = c("lightgray", "lightblue", "lightgreen"),
  ylab = "Rep-to-rep correlation",
  main = "nor23 yld5: Spatial Correction Comparison",
  ylim = c(0,1)
)

# Summary
aggregate(Correlation ~ Model, df_all_yld5_nor23, mean)
aggregate(Correlation ~ Model, df_all_yld5_nor23, sd)
```

```{r Combined chunk for harvest6 using Random Regression 04282026}
# ---------- PART 0: Manange data file -----------

#  Manage data file: First, assign harvest based on GDD
# first make harvest6 only data file
nmsu23_nor_pheno_gndvi_only_long_harvestwise <- 
  nmsu23_nor_pheno_gndvi_only_long %>%
  mutate(Harvest = case_when(
    # no harvest 1 in this treatment
    GDD >= 119 & GDD <= 153 ~ "Harvest2", # here upper limit is of actual yld
    GDD >= 153 & GDD <= 181 ~ "Harvest3",
    GDD >= 181 & GDD <= 207 ~ "Harvest4",
    GDD >= 207 & GDD <= 243 ~ "harvest5",
    GDD >= 243 & GDD <= 279 ~ "Harvest6",
    GDD >= 279 & GDD <= 310 ~ "Harvest7"
  ))

# Subset harvest6
nmsu23_nor_gdd_harvest6 <- nmsu23_nor_pheno_gndvi_only_long_harvestwise %>%
  filter(Harvest == "Harvest6") # !!! capital H

# create factor + numeric GDD
nmsu23_nor_gdd_harvest6$GDD_fac <- as.factor(nmsu23_nor_gdd_harvest6$GDD)
nmsu23_nor_gdd_harvest6 <- nmsu23_nor_gdd_harvest6[order(nmsu23_nor_gdd_harvest6$GDD_fac),]

unique(nmsu23_nor_gdd_harvest6$GDD_fac) # 257 263 278 279(for yld6)

# Build Legendre basis
unique_gdd_yld6 <- sort(unique(nmsu23_nor_gdd_harvest6$GDD))
unique_gdd_yld6 <- as.numeric(unique_gdd_yld6)

 ######## fitting linear equation
M_yld6 <- stdtime(unique_gdd_yld6, 1) # for linear, 1
lambda_yld6 <- Legendre(1, gengler=TRUE) # for linear, 1 (intercept + slope)

Phi_yld6 <- M_yld6 %*% t(lambda_yld6)
colnames(Phi_yld6) <- c("LPInt", "LPLin")
rownames(Phi_yld6) <- unique_gdd_yld6
Phi_yld6
ordLP_yld6 <- match(nmsu23_nor_gdd_harvest6$GDD, rownames(Phi_yld6))
nmsu23_nor_gdd_harvest6$LPInt_yld6 <- Phi_yld6[ordLP_yld6, "LPInt"]
nmsu23_nor_gdd_harvest6$LPLin_yld6 <- Phi_yld6[ordLP_yld6, "LPLin"]

# Fit RR model (harvest 1)
asreml.options(extra = 200, maxit = 200)

lp_mod_nor_23_yld6 <- { 
  attr(grm_inverse, "INVERSE") <- TRUE
  asreml(
    fixed = GNDVI ~ 1 + at(GDD_fac):Rep,
    random = ~ str(~ Germplasm:LPInt_yld6 + Germplasm:LPLin_yld6, ~ us(2):vm(Germplasm, grm_inverse)) + str(~ Plot:LPInt_yld6 + Plot:LPLin_yld6, ~ us(2):id(Plot)),
    residual = ~ dsum(~ units | GDD_fac),
    data = nmsu23_nor_gdd_harvest6)}

summary(lp_mod_nor_23_yld6)$varcomp
lp_mod_nor_23_yld6 <- update.asreml(lp_mod_nor_23_yld6, start = lp_mod_nor_23_yld6$gammas)

# Save random effects (BLUPs)
blups_yld6 <- lp_mod_nor_23_yld6$coefficients$random
blups_yld6

# --- Convert full BLUPs to a data frame ---
blups_df_yld6 <- as.data.frame(blups_yld6) %>% rename(solution = 1)
blups_df_yld6
# Add term names (simplify)
blups_df_yld6$term <- gsub(":.*", "", rownames(blups_df_yld6))

# --- Filter subsets ---
# BLUP_germplasm_yld6 <- blups_df_yld6 %>% filter(grepl("^Germplasm", rownames(blups_df_yld6)))
BLUP_spa_int_yld6 <- blups_df_yld6 %>% 
  filter(grepl("^Plot_.*LPInt_yld6$", rownames(blups_df_yld6)))

BLUP_spa_slp_yld6 <- blups_df_yld6 %>%
```

### 2. GEER
 - NOTE: yld#, PEE_###, Check AR model (full or 1D)

```{r GEER between all rep combinations for yld6 Nor 2023, 04282026}
### ---------------------------------------------------------
### 1. Function: Fit model and extract genomic BLUPs
### ---------------------------------------------------------
get_gblup_yld6_nor23 <- function(dat, model_type = c("base", "spa", "pee"), grm_inverse) {
  
  # Ensure GRM is treated as inverse relationship matrix
  attr(grm_inverse, "INVERSE") <- TRUE
  
  # Match model type argument
  model_type <- match.arg(model_type)

  # ---------------------------------------------------------
  # Fit model (robust to failure)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------
  fit <- tryCatch({
    
    if (model_type == "base") {
      # Baseline genomic model (no spatial/environmental correction)
      asreml(
        fixed   = yld6 ~ 1 , # we dont need rep here cz the data is only for one rep
        random  = ~ vm(Germplasm, grm_inverse),
        residual= ~ id(units),
        data    = dat
      )
      
    } else if (model_type == "spa") {
      # Genomic model + 2D autoregressive spatial structure
      asreml(
        fixed   = yld6 ~ 1 , # we dont need rep here cz the data is only for one rep
        random  = ~ vm(Germplasm, grm_inverse) + ar1(Row):ar1(Range),
        residual= ~ id(units),
        data    = dat
      )
      
    } else if (model_type == "pee") {
      # Genomic model + permanent environmental effect (PEE)
      asreml(
        fixed   = yld6 ~ 1 + PEE_279, #!!! PEE
        random  = ~ vm(Germplasm, grm_inverse),
        residual= ~ id(units),
        data    = dat
      )
    }
    
  }, error = function(e) NULL)   # Return NULL if model fails

  # If model fitting failed → skip
  if (is.null(fit)) return(NULL)

  # ---------------------------------------------------------
  # Extract genomic BLUPs (u_a)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------
  blup <- tryCatch(coef(fit)$random, error = function(e) NULL)
  
  # If extraction failed → skip
  if (is.null(blup)) return(NULL)

  # Keep only Germplasm effects
  blup <- blup[grep("Germplasm", rownames(blup)), , drop = FALSE]
  
  # If no genetic effects found → skip
  if (nrow(blup) == 0) return(NULL)

  # Convert to named numeric vector
  out <- blup[, 1]
  names(out) <- rownames(blup)

  return(out)
}


### ---------------------------------------------------------
### 2. Function: Compute GEER across all replicate pairs
### ---------------------------------------------------------
geer_all_pairs_yld6_nor23 <- function(dat, grm_inverse, rep_col = "Rep") {
  
  # Split dataset by replicate
  rep_list <- split(dat, dat[[rep_col]])
  rep_names <- names(rep_list)
  
  # All pairwise replicate combinations
  pairs <- combn(rep_names, 2, simplify = FALSE)

  # Loop over replicate pairs
  res <- lapply(pairs, function(p) {
    
    d1 <- rep_list[[p[1]]]
    d2 <- rep_list[[p[2]]]

    models <- c("base", "spa", "pee")

    # Compute GEER for each model
    pair_res <- lapply(models, function(m) {
      
      g1 <- get_gblup_yld6_nor23(d1, m, grm_inverse)
      g2 <- get_gblup_yld6_nor23(d2, m, grm_inverse)

      # Skip if either replicate failed
      if (is.null(g1) || is.null(g2)) return(NULL)

      # Align common germplasm entries
      common_ids <- intersect(names(g1), names(g2))
      if (length(common_ids) < 2) return(NULL)

      # Compute correlations
      pear <- tryCatch(
        cor(g1[common_ids], g2[common_ids]),
        error = function(e) NA_real_
      )
      
      spear <- tryCatch(
        cor(g1[common_ids], g2[common_ids], method = "spearman"),
        error = function(e) NA_real_
      )

      # Return results
      data.frame(
        Rep1 = p[1],
        Rep2 = p[2],
        Model = m,
        N_common = length(common_ids),
        Pearson = pear,
        Spearman = spear,
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      )
    })

    do.call(rbind, pair_res)
  })

  # Combine all results
  res <- do.call(rbind, res)
  rownames(res) <- NULL

  return(res)
}


### ---------------------------------------------------------
### 3. Run GEER analysis
### ---------------------------------------------------------
GEER_results_yld6_nor23 <- geer_all_pairs_yld6_nor23(
  nmsu23_nor_pheno,
  grm_inverse
)

GEER_results_yld6_nor23


### ---------------------------------------------------------
### 4. Summary statistics
### ---------------------------------------------------------

# Number of valid comparisons per model
table(GEER_results_yld6_nor23$Model)

# Mean GEER per model
aggregate(
  cbind(Pearson, Spearman) ~ Model,
  GEER_results_yld6_nor23,
  mean
)


### ---------------------------------------------------------
### 5. Visualization: GEER (Pearson)
### ---------------------------------------------------------

# Ensure consistent ordering for plotting
GEER_results_yld6_nor23$Model <- factor(
  GEER_results_yld6_nor23$Model,
  levels = c("base", "spa", "pee"),
  labels = c("Base", "Spa(AR)", "PEE"))

# Boxplot of Pearson GEER
boxplot(
  Pearson ~ Model,
  data = GEER_results_yld6_nor23,
  col = c("grey70", "skyblue", "tomato"),
  border = "black",
  ylab = "GEER (Pearson correlation)",
  xlab = "Model",
  main = "Genotypic Effect Estimation across Replicates (GEER)\nHarvest 6, NOR 2023",
  outline = TRUE
)

# Overlay individual replicate-pair estimates
stripchart(
  Pearson ~ Model,
  data = GEER_results_yld6_nor23,
  vertical = TRUE,
  method = "jitter",
  pch = 19,
  col = "black",
  add = TRUE
)
```

###  Spatially Corrected Rep-wise Yield Correlation (SCRYC)
 - correlation of phenotypes/yield after removing spatial effects across reps
- PEE much better cz autoreg.is not capturing
```{r  Spatially Corrected Yiled, yld6, 04282026}
# ============================================================
# NEW METRIC: SPATIALLY CORRECTED YIELD (yld6_nor23)
# ============================================================

# -------------------------------
# 1. PREPARE WORKING DATA
# -------------------------------
nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC <- nmsu23_nor_pheno

# ============================================================
# 1.1 SPATIAL (AR1): EXTRACT + ALIGN SPATIAL BLUPS
# ============================================================

# Extract all random effects
spa_blup_yld6_nor23 <- uni_nmsu23_nor_yld6_spa$coefficients$random
spa_blup_yld6_nor23
# Extract ONLY Row:Range spatial effects (correct pattern)
spa_eff_yld6_nor23 <- spa_blup_yld6_nor23[
  grep("^Row_[0-9]+:Range_[0-9]+", rownames(spa_blup_yld6_nor23)),
  , drop = FALSE]
spa_eff_yld6_nor23

# Build lookup table (use column name "effect")
spa_df_yld6_nor23 <- data.frame(
  RowRange = rownames(spa_eff_yld6_nor23),
  spa_eff_yld6_nor23 = spa_eff_yld6_nor23[,"effect"],
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
spa_df_yld6_nor23
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Create matching key in phenotype data
# ------------------------------------------------------------
nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$RowRange <- paste0(
  "Row_", nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$Row,
  ":Range_", nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$Range)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Match WITHOUT reordering (IMPORTANT)
# ------------------------------------------------------------

match_idx <- match(
  nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$RowRange,
  spa_df_yld6_nor23$RowRange)

nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$spa_eff_yld6_nor23 <- 
  spa_df_yld6_nor23$spa_eff_yld6_nor23[match_idx]
 # i doubled check the spatial blups and these columns to make sure i am getting what i wanted

# Sanity check (must be zero)
sum(is.na(nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$spa_eff_yld6_nor23)) # 0

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Corrected yield (AR1)
# ------------------------------------------------------------

nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$yld6_spa_corr_nor23 <- 
  nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$yld6 - nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$spa_eff_yld6_nor23




# ============================================================
# 1.2 PEE: DIRECT SPATIAL CORRECTION
# ============================================================

 # we need to scale PEE to be able to use it for spatial correction

# lets see
# Extract coefficient
beta_pee_yld6_nor23 <- uni_nmsu23_nor_yld6_pee$coefficients$fixed["PEE_279", "effect"]
beta_pee_yld6_nor23   #  

# Apply correct spatial correction
nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$yld6_pee_corr_nor23 <- 
  nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$yld6 - 
  beta_pee_yld6_nor23 * nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$PEE_279


# ============================================================
# 2. REP-WISE CORRELATIONS
# ============================================================

# -------------------------------
# SPLIT DATA BY REP
# -------------------------------

rep1_yld6_nor23 <- nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC[nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$Rep == 1, ]
dim(nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC) # 144*85
dim(rep1_yld6_nor23) # should be 144/4 = 36 and it is. JUST SANITY CHECK
rep2_yld6_nor23 <- nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC[nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$Rep == 2, ]
rep3_yld6_nor23 <- nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC[nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$Rep == 3, ]
rep4_yld6_nor23 <- nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC[nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$Rep == 4, ]

# Align by genotype
rep1_yld6_nor23 <- rep1_yld6_nor23[order(rep1_yld6_nor23$Germplasm), ]
rep2_yld6_nor23 <- rep2_yld6_nor23[order(rep2_yld6_nor23$Germplasm), ]
rep3_yld6_nor23 <- rep3_yld6_nor23[order(rep3_yld6_nor23$Germplasm), ]
rep4_yld6_nor23 <- rep4_yld6_nor23[order(rep4_yld6_nor23$Germplasm), ]


# ============================================================
# 1. RAW YIELD
# ============================================================

cor_raw_yld6_nor23 <- c(
  cor(rep1_yld6_nor23$yld6, rep2_yld6_nor23$yld6, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep1_yld6_nor23$yld6, rep3_yld6_nor23$yld6, use="complete.obs"),

  cor(rep2_yld6_nor23$yld6, rep4_yld6_nor23$yld6, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep3_yld6_nor23$yld6, rep4_yld6_nor23$yld6, use="complete.obs") )

df_raw_yld6_nor23 <- data.frame(
  Model = "Raw",
  Correlation = cor_raw_yld6_nor23)
df_raw_yld6_nor23

# ============================================================
# 2. AR1 CORRECTED
# ============================================================

cor_spa_cor_yld6_nor23 <- c(
  cor(rep1_yld6_nor23$yld6_spa_corr_nor23, rep2_yld6_nor23$yld6_spa_corr_nor23, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep1_yld6_nor23$yld6_spa_corr_nor23, rep3_yld6_nor23$yld6_spa_corr_nor23, use="complete.obs"),

df_spa_yld6_nor23 <- data.frame(
```

```{r Combined chunk for harvest7 using Random Regression 04282026}
# ---------- PART 0: Manange data file -----------

#  Manage data file: First, assign harvest based on GDD
# first make harvest7 only data file
nmsu23_nor_pheno_gndvi_only_long_harvestwise <- 
  nmsu23_nor_pheno_gndvi_only_long %>%
  mutate(Harvest = case_when(
    # no harvest 1 in this treatment
    GDD >= 119 & GDD <= 153 ~ "Harvest2", # here upper limit is of actual yld
    GDD >= 153 & GDD <= 181 ~ "Harvest3",
    GDD >= 181 & GDD <= 207 ~ "Harvest4",
    GDD >= 207 & GDD <= 243 ~ "harvest5",
    GDD >= 243 & GDD <= 279 ~ "Harvest6",
    GDD >= 279 & GDD <= 310 ~ "Harvest7"
  ))

# Subset harvest7
nmsu23_nor_gdd_harvest7 <- nmsu23_nor_pheno_gndvi_only_long_harvestwise %>%
  filter(Harvest == "Harvest7") # !!! capital H

# create factor + numeric GDD
nmsu23_nor_gdd_harvest7$GDD_fac <- as.factor(nmsu23_nor_gdd_harvest7$GDD)
nmsu23_nor_gdd_harvest7 <- nmsu23_nor_gdd_harvest7[order(nmsu23_nor_gdd_harvest7$GDD_fac),]

unique(nmsu23_nor_gdd_harvest7$GDD_fac) # 293 299 307(for yld7)

# Build Legendre basis
unique_gdd_yld7 <- sort(unique(nmsu23_nor_gdd_harvest7$GDD))
unique_gdd_yld7 <- as.numeric(unique_gdd_yld7)

 ######## fitting linear equation
M_yld7 <- stdtime(unique_gdd_yld7, 1) # for linear, 1
lambda_yld7 <- Legendre(1, gengler=TRUE) # for linear, 1 (intercept + slope)

Phi_yld7 <- M_yld7 %*% t(lambda_yld7)
colnames(Phi_yld7) <- c("LPInt", "LPLin")
rownames(Phi_yld7) <- unique_gdd_yld7
Phi_yld7
ordLP_yld7 <- match(nmsu23_nor_gdd_harvest7$GDD, rownames(Phi_yld7))
nmsu23_nor_gdd_harvest7$LPInt_yld7 <- Phi_yld7[ordLP_yld7, "LPInt"]
nmsu23_nor_gdd_harvest7$LPLin_yld7 <- Phi_yld7[ordLP_yld7, "LPLin"]

# Fit RR model (harvest 1)
asreml.options(extra = 200, maxit = 200)

lp_mod_nor_23_yld7 <- { 
  attr(grm_inverse, "INVERSE") <- TRUE
  asreml(
    fixed = GNDVI ~ 1 + at(GDD_fac):Rep,
    random = ~ str(~ Germplasm:LPInt_yld7 + Germplasm:LPLin_yld7, ~ us(2):vm(Germplasm, grm_inverse)) + str(~ Plot:LPInt_yld7 + Plot:LPLin_yld7, ~ us(2):id(Plot)),
    residual = ~ dsum(~ units | GDD_fac),
    data = nmsu23_nor_gdd_harvest7)}

summary(lp_mod_nor_23_yld7)$varcomp
lp_mod_nor_23_yld7 <- update.asreml(lp_mod_nor_23_yld7, start = lp_mod_nor_23_yld7$gammas)

# Save random effects (BLUPs)
blups_yld7 <- lp_mod_nor_23_yld7$coefficients$random
blups_yld7

# --- Convert full BLUPs to a data frame ---
blups_df_yld7 <- as.data.frame(blups_yld7) %>% rename(solution = 1)
blups_df_yld7
# Add term names (simplify)
blups_df_yld7$term <- gsub(":.*", "", rownames(blups_df_yld7))

# --- Filter subsets ---
# BLUP_germplasm_yld7 <- blups_df_yld7 %>% filter(grepl("^Germplasm", rownames(blups_df_yld7)))
BLUP_spa_int_yld7 <- blups_df_yld7 %>% 
  filter(grepl("^Plot_.*LPInt_yld7$", rownames(blups_df_yld7)))

BLUP_spa_slp_yld7 <- blups_df_yld7 %>% 
  filter(grepl("^Plot_.*LPLin_yld7$", rownames(blups_df_yld7)))

# --- Spatial BLUPs ---
BLUP_spa_int_yld7$solution   # Intercepts
BLUP_spa_slp_yld7$solution   # Slopes

# --- Combine intercept and slope into a matrix ---
spa_BLUP_matrix_yld7 <- cbind(
  BLUP_spa_int_yld7$solution, 
  BLUP_spa_slp_yld7$solution)
spa_BLUP_matrix_yld7

# ---------- Extract spatial BLUPs as PEE (Permanent Environmental Effects) ----------

# Convert matrix into a data frame for including it in the model below cz my model expects columns in the data frame
nmsu23_nor_spa_yld7 <- as.data.frame(spa_BLUP_matrix_yld7)
# add these as columns in my data file
nmsu23_nor_pheno$spa_int_yld7 <- nmsu23_nor_spa_yld7[,1]
nmsu23_nor_pheno$spa_slp_yld7 <- nmsu23_nor_spa_yld7[,2]

# !!!!!!!!!!!!!!! Permanent Environmental Effect !!!!!!!!!!!!! 
Phi_yld7
# here intercept and slope for GDD on PEE_310 are 1 and 1.7320508 
nmsu23_nor_pheno$PEE_310 <- 
  1 * nmsu23_nor_pheno$spa_int_yld7 +
  1.7320508 * nmsu23_nor_pheno$spa_slp_yld7


# ---------- Step 2: Fit PEE's as fixed regressor on a yield model with spatial correction ----------

# Fit single-trait model for yield (yld7)
```
