### 2. GEER
 - NOTE: yld#, PEE_###, Check AR model (full or 1D)

```{r GEER between all rep combinations for yld7 Nor 2023, 04282026}
### ---------------------------------------------------------
### 1. Function: Fit model and extract genomic BLUPs
### ---------------------------------------------------------
get_gblup_yld7_nor23 <- function(dat, model_type = c("base", "spa", "pee"), grm_inverse) {
  
  # Ensure GRM is treated as inverse relationship matrix
  attr(grm_inverse, "INVERSE") <- TRUE
  
  # Match model type argument
  model_type <- match.arg(model_type)

  # ---------------------------------------------------------
  # Fit model (robust to failure)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------
  fit <- tryCatch({
    
    if (model_type == "base") {
      # Baseline genomic model (no spatial/environmental correction)
      asreml(
        fixed   = yld7 ~ 1 , # we dont need rep here cz the data is only for one rep
        random  = ~ vm(Germplasm, grm_inverse),
        residual= ~ id(units),
        data    = dat
      )
      
    } else if (model_type == "spa") {
      # Genomic model + 2D autoregressive spatial structure
      asreml(
        fixed   = yld7 ~ 1 , # we dont need rep here cz the data is only for one rep
        random  = ~ vm(Germplasm, grm_inverse) + ar1(Row),
        residual= ~ id(units),
        data    = dat
      )
      
    } else if (model_type == "pee") {
      # Genomic model + permanent environmental effect (PEE)
      asreml(
        fixed   = yld7 ~ 1 + PEE_310, #!!! PEE
        random  = ~ vm(Germplasm, grm_inverse),
        residual= ~ id(units),
        data    = dat
      )
    }
    
  }, error = function(e) NULL)   # Return NULL if model fails

  # If model fitting failed → skip
  if (is.null(fit)) return(NULL)

  # ---------------------------------------------------------
  # Extract genomic BLUPs (u_a)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------
  blup <- tryCatch(coef(fit)$random, error = function(e) NULL)
  
  # If extraction failed → skip
  if (is.null(blup)) return(NULL)

  # Keep only Germplasm effects
  blup <- blup[grep("Germplasm", rownames(blup)), , drop = FALSE]
  
  # If no genetic effects found → skip
  if (nrow(blup) == 0) return(NULL)

  # Convert to named numeric vector
  out <- blup[, 1]
  names(out) <- rownames(blup)

  return(out)
}


### ---------------------------------------------------------
### 2. Function: Compute GEER across all replicate pairs
### ---------------------------------------------------------
geer_all_pairs_yld7_nor23 <- function(dat, grm_inverse, rep_col = "Rep") {
  
  # Split dataset by replicate
  rep_list <- split(dat, dat[[rep_col]])
  rep_names <- names(rep_list)
  
  # All pairwise replicate combinations
  pairs <- combn(rep_names, 2, simplify = FALSE)

  # Loop over replicate pairs
  res <- lapply(pairs, function(p) {
    
    d1 <- rep_list[[p[1]]]
    d2 <- rep_list[[p[2]]]

    models <- c("base", "spa", "pee")

    # Compute GEER for each model
    pair_res <- lapply(models, function(m) {
      
      g1 <- get_gblup_yld7_nor23(d1, m, grm_inverse)
      g2 <- get_gblup_yld7_nor23(d2, m, grm_inverse)

      # Skip if either replicate failed
      if (is.null(g1) || is.null(g2)) return(NULL)

      # Align common germplasm entries
      common_ids <- intersect(names(g1), names(g2))
      if (length(common_ids) < 2) return(NULL)

      # Compute correlations
      pear <- tryCatch(
        cor(g1[common_ids], g2[common_ids]),
        error = function(e) NA_real_
      )
      
      spear <- tryCatch(
        cor(g1[common_ids], g2[common_ids], method = "spearman"),
        error = function(e) NA_real_
      )

      # Return results
      data.frame(
        Rep1 = p[1],
        Rep2 = p[2],
        Model = m,
        N_common = length(common_ids),
        Pearson = pear,
        Spearman = spear,
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      )
    })

    do.call(rbind, pair_res)
  })

  # Combine all results
  res <- do.call(rbind, res)
  rownames(res) <- NULL

  return(res)
}


### ---------------------------------------------------------
### 3. Run GEER analysis
### ---------------------------------------------------------
GEER_results_yld7_nor23 <- geer_all_pairs_yld7_nor23(
  nmsu23_nor_pheno,
  grm_inverse
)

GEER_results_yld7_nor23


### ---------------------------------------------------------
### 4. Summary statistics
### ---------------------------------------------------------

# Number of valid comparisons per model
table(GEER_results_yld7_nor23$Model)

# Mean GEER per model
aggregate(
  cbind(Pearson, Spearman) ~ Model,
  GEER_results_yld7_nor23,
  mean
)


### ---------------------------------------------------------
### 5. Visualization: GEER (Pearson)
### ---------------------------------------------------------

# Ensure consistent ordering for plotting
GEER_results_yld7_nor23$Model <- factor(
  GEER_results_yld7_nor23$Model,
  levels = c("base", "spa", "pee"),
  labels = c("Base", "Spa(AR)", "PEE"))

# Boxplot of Pearson GEER
boxplot(
  Pearson ~ Model,
  data = GEER_results_yld7_nor23,
  col = c("grey70", "skyblue", "tomato"),
  border = "black",
  ylab = "GEER (Pearson correlation)",
  xlab = "Model",
  main = "Genotypic Effect Estimation across Replicates (GEER)\nHarvest 7, NOR 2023",
  outline = TRUE
)

# Overlay individual replicate-pair estimates
stripchart(
  Pearson ~ Model,
  data = GEER_results_yld7_nor23,
  vertical = TRUE,
  method = "jitter",
  pch = 19,
  col = "black",
  add = TRUE
)
```

###  Spatially Corrected Rep-wise Yield Correlation (SCRYC)
 - correlation of phenotypes/yield after removing spatial effects across reps
- PEE much better cz autoreg.is not capturing
```{r  Spatially Corrected Yiled, yld7, 04282026}
# ============================================================
# NEW METRIC: SPATIALLY CORRECTED YIELD (yld7_nor23)
# ============================================================

# -------------------------------
# 1. PREPARE WORKING DATA
# -------------------------------
nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC <- nmsu23_nor_pheno

# ============================================================
# 1.1 SPATIAL (AR1): EXTRACT + ALIGN SPATIAL BLUPS
# ============================================================

# Extract all random effects
spa_blup_yld7_nor23 <- uni_nmsu23_nor_yld7_spa$coefficients$random
spa_blup_yld7_nor23
# Extract ONLY Row:Range spatial effects (correct pattern)
spa_eff_yld7_nor23 <- spa_blup_yld7_nor23[
  grep("^Row_[0-9]+:Range_[0-9]+", rownames(spa_blup_yld7_nor23)),
  , drop = FALSE]
spa_eff_yld7_nor23

# Build lookup table (use column name "effect")
spa_df_yld7_nor23 <- data.frame(
  RowRange = rownames(spa_eff_yld7_nor23),
  spa_eff_yld7_nor23 = spa_eff_yld7_nor23[,"effect"],
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
spa_df_yld7_nor23
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Create matching key in phenotype data
# ------------------------------------------------------------
nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$RowRange <- paste0(
  "Row_", nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$Row,
  ":Range_", nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$Range)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Match WITHOUT reordering (IMPORTANT)
# ------------------------------------------------------------

match_idx <- match(
  nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$RowRange,
  spa_df_yld7_nor23$RowRange)

nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$spa_eff_yld7_nor23 <- 
  spa_df_yld7_nor23$spa_eff_yld7_nor23[match_idx]
 # i doubled check the spatial blups and these columns to make sure i am getting what i wanted

# Sanity check (must be zero)
sum(is.na(nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$spa_eff_yld7_nor23)) # 0

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Corrected yield (AR1)
# ------------------------------------------------------------

nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$yld7_spa_corr_nor23 <- 
  nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$yld7 - nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$spa_eff_yld7_nor23




# ============================================================
# 1.2 PEE: DIRECT SPATIAL CORRECTION
# ============================================================

 # we need to scale PEE to be able to use it for spatial correction

# lets see
# Extract coefficient
beta_pee_yld7_nor23 <- uni_nmsu23_nor_yld7_pee$coefficients$fixed["PEE_310", "effect"]
beta_pee_yld7_nor23   #  

# Apply correct spatial correction
nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$yld7_pee_corr_nor23 <- 
  nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$yld7 - 
  beta_pee_yld7_nor23 * nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$PEE_310


# ============================================================
# 2. REP-WISE CORRELATIONS
# ============================================================

# -------------------------------
# SPLIT DATA BY REP
# -------------------------------

rep1_yld7_nor23 <- nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC[nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$Rep == 1, ]
dim(nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC) # 144*88
dim(rep1_yld7_nor23) # should be 144/4 = 36 and it is. JUST SANITY CHECK
rep2_yld7_nor23 <- nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC[nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$Rep == 2, ]
rep3_yld7_nor23 <- nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC[nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$Rep == 3, ]
rep4_yld7_nor23 <- nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC[nmsu23_nor_pheno_SC$Rep == 4, ]

# Align by genotype

rep2_yld7_nor23 <- rep2_yld7_nor23[order(rep2_yld7_nor23$Germplasm), ]
rep3_yld7_nor23 <- rep3_yld7_nor23[order(rep3_yld7_nor23$Germplasm), ]
rep4_yld7_nor23 <- rep4_yld7_nor23[order(rep4_yld7_nor23$Germplasm), ]


# ============================================================

# ============================================================

cor_raw_yld7_nor23 <- c(
  cor(rep1_yld7_nor23$yld7, rep2_yld7_nor23$yld7, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep1_yld7_nor23$yld7, rep3_yld7_nor23$yld7, use="complete.obs"),

df_pee_yld7_nor23

# ============================================================

aggregate(Correlation ~ Model, df_all_yld7_nor23, sd)
```

# Metrics as Baseline deviation (for cor, GEER, validation of GEER:
## 1. Metrics as Baseline deviation: ΔGEER 

GEER as deviation, ΔGEER
yld2
- in each rep, we do the subtraction
```{r yld2, GEER deviation, nor23, 04282026}
## ============================================================
## yld2: Compute GEER deviation (ΔGEER) relative to baseline
## nor23
## ============================================================

## ------------------------------------------------------------
## Step 1: Inspect input GEER results
## ------------------------------------------------------------
GEER_results_yld2_nor23


## ------------------------------------------------------------
## Step 2: Convert to wide format
## Each row = replicate pair
## Columns = Base, Spa(AR), PEE
## ------------------------------------------------------------
df_wide_yld2_nor23 <- GEER_results_yld2_nor23 %>%
  dplyr::select(Rep1, Rep2, Model, Pearson) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = Model, values_from = Pearson)


## ------------------------------------------------------------
## Step 3: Compute deviation from baseline (ΔGEER)
## AR  = Spa(AR) − Base
## RR  = PEE − Base
## ------------------------------------------------------------
df_delta_yld2_nor23 <- df_wide_yld2_nor23 %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    AR = `Spa(AR)` - Base,
    RR = PEE - Base)


## ------------------------------------------------------------
## Step 4: Convert to long format for plotting
## ------------------------------------------------------------
df_plot_yld2_nor23 <- df_delta_yld2_nor23 %>%
  dplyr::select(Rep1, Rep2, AR, RR) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = c(AR, RR),
    names_to = "Model",
    values_to = "Delta")


## ------------------------------------------------------------
## Step 5: Ensure consistent model order
## ------------------------------------------------------------
df_plot_yld2_nor23$Model <- factor(
  df_plot_yld2_nor23$Model,
  levels = c("AR", "RR"))


## ------------------------------------------------------------
## Step 6: Boxplot of ΔGEER
## ------------------------------------------------------------
boxplot(
  Delta ~ Model,
  data = df_plot_yld2_nor23,
  col = c("skyblue", "tomato"),
  boxwex = 0.3,  # default ≈ 0.8 → reduce this
  ylab = expression(Delta~GEER),
  main = "yld2: Improvement over Baseline (ΔGEER)")
abline(h = 0, lty = 2)


```

## 2. Deviation based for cor: ΔCOR → correlation(fitted, observed) 

```{r ΔCOR nor23, 04282026}
## ============================================================
## ΔCOR: Fit vs Observed correlation (relative to Base)
## nor23
## ============================================================

## ------------------------------------------------------------
## Step 1: Create table manually (per yield)
## ------------------------------------------------------------

cor_nor23 <- data.frame(
  Harvest = paste0("YLD", 2:7), # yld starts from 2 here
  Base = c(
    cor_fit_obs_base_yld2_NOR23,
    cor_fit_obs_base_yld3_NOR23,
    cor_fit_obs_base_yld4_NOR23,
    cor_fit_obs_base_yld5_NOR23,
    cor_fit_obs_base_yld6_NOR23,
    cor_fit_obs_base_yld7_NOR23),
  AR = c(
    cor_fit_obs_spa_yld2_NOR23,
    cor_fit_obs_spa_yld3_NOR23,
    cor_fit_obs_spa_yld4_NOR23,
    cor_fit_obs_spa_yld5_NOR23,
    cor_fit_obs_spa_yld6_NOR23,
    cor_fit_obs_spa_yld7_NOR23),
  RR = c(
    cor_fit_obs_pee_yld2_NOR23,
    cor_fit_obs_pee_yld3_NOR23,
    cor_fit_obs_pee_yld4_NOR23,
    cor_fit_obs_pee_yld5_NOR23,
    cor_fit_obs_pee_yld6_NOR23,
    cor_fit_obs_pee_yld7_NOR23))

## ------------------------------------------------------------
## Step 2: Compute ΔCOR
## ------------------------------------------------------------
cor_delta_nor23 <- cor_nor23 %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    AR = AR - Base, # here AR-base
    RR = RR - Base) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = c(AR, RR),
    names_to = "Model",
    values_to = "Delta")

cor_delta_nor23$Model <- factor(cor_delta_nor23$Model, levels = c("AR","RR"))


## ------------------------------------------------------------
## Step 3: Plot
## ------------------------------------------------------------
ggplot(cor_delta_nor23, aes(Model, Delta, fill = Model)) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.2, alpha = 0.3) +
  #geom_jitter(width = 0.05, size = 2) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point", shape = 18, size = 3, color = "red") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  ylab(expression(Delta~COR)) +
  ggtitle("nor23: All Harvests- Fitted vs Observed Yields (ΔCOR)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

Normally if the range of numbers vary a lot between vi's and yield, then we can scale yield to variance level of vi's. but here since yield is in lb and upto 2 digit, should have that issue. If got any, we can always use scaled yield.
```{r scaling yield }
# we only have to scale 6 harvest values based on gndvi's value. Of course the variance between VI's differ but it should be okay to use Yield scaled onto gndvi for analysis with NDRE and Ggndvi as well. 

# Define the mapping of yield traits to gndvi columns
yield_traits <- paste0("yld", 2:6)
gndvi_times <- c("GNDVI_152", "GNDVI_179", "GNDVI_206", "GNDVI_278", "GNDVI_307") # selecting one of the time point closest to each harvest window. selecting based on higher variation time point from heatmap, not actually calculating all. FOR this check the harvest windows or pheno cor heatmaps to see which time point falls in which window

# Loop over each yield trait
for (i in 1:length(yield_traits)) {
  
  trait <- yield_traits[i]
  gndvi_col <- gndvi_times[i]
  
  # Calculate variance of gndvi and yield
  gndvi_var <- var(nmsu23_et_pheno[[gndvi_col]], na.rm = TRUE)
  yld_var <- var(nmsu23_et_pheno[[trait]], na.rm = TRUE)
  
  # Calculate scaling factor
  sf <- sqrt(gndvi_var) / sqrt(yld_var)
  
  # Create new scaled yield column
  new_col <- paste0("sca_", trait)
  nmsu23_et_pheno[[new_col]] <- nmsu23_et_pheno[[trait]] * sf
  
  #  Print scaling factor
  cat("Scaling factor for", trait, "using", gndvi_col, ":", sf, "\n")
}


# thus all scaled yields are added as a new column at last. 
```

### 2. GEER
 - NOTE: yld#, PEE_###, Check AR model (full or 1D)

```{r GEER between all rep combinations for yld2 et 2023, 04282026}
### ---------------------------------------------------------
### 1. Function: Fit model and extract genomic BLUPs
### ---------------------------------------------------------
get_gblup_yld2_et23 <- function(dat, model_type = c("base", "spa", "pee"), grm_inverse) {
  
  # Ensure GRM is treated as inverse relationship matrix
  attr(grm_inverse, "INVERSE") <- TRUE
  
  # Match model type argument
  model_type <- match.arg(model_type)

  # ---------------------------------------------------------
  # Fit model (robust to failure)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------
  fit <- tryCatch({
    
    if (model_type == "base") {
      # Baseline genomic model (no spatial/environmental correction)
      asreml(
        fixed   = yld2 ~ 1 , # we dont need rep here cz the data is only for one rep
        random  = ~ vm(Germplasm, grm_inverse),
        residual= ~ id(units),
        data    = dat
      )
      
    } else if (model_type == "spa") {
      # Genomic model + 2D autoregressive spatial structure
      asreml(
        fixed   = yld2 ~ 1 , # we dont need rep here cz the data is only for one rep
        random  = ~ vm(Germplasm, grm_inverse) + ar1(Row):ar1(Range),
        residual= ~ id(units),
        data    = dat
      )
      
    } else if (model_type == "pee") {
      # Genomic model + permanent environmental effect (PEE)
      asreml(
        fixed   = yld2 ~ 1 + PEE_153,
        random  = ~ vm(Germplasm, grm_inverse),
        residual= ~ id(units),
        data    = dat
      )
    }
    
  }, error = function(e) NULL)   # Return NULL if model fails

  # If model fitting failed → skip
  if (is.null(fit)) return(NULL)

  # ---------------------------------------------------------
  # Extract genomic BLUPs (u_a)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------
  blup <- tryCatch(coef(fit)$random, error = function(e) NULL)
  
  # If extraction failed → skip
  if (is.null(blup)) return(NULL)

  # Keep only Germplasm effects
  blup <- blup[grep("Germplasm", rownames(blup)), , drop = FALSE]
  
  # If no genetic effects found → skip
  if (nrow(blup) == 0) return(NULL)

  # Convert to named numeric vector
  out <- blup[, 1]
  names(out) <- rownames(blup)

  return(out)
}


### ---------------------------------------------------------
### 2. Function: Compute GEER across all replicate pairs
### ---------------------------------------------------------
geer_all_pairs_yld2_et23 <- function(dat, grm_inverse, rep_col = "Rep") {
  
  # Split dataset by replicate
  rep_list <- split(dat, dat[[rep_col]])
  rep_names <- names(rep_list)
  
  # All pairwise replicate combinations
  pairs <- combn(rep_names, 2, simplify = FALSE)

  # Loop over replicate pairs
  res <- lapply(pairs, function(p) {
    
    d1 <- rep_list[[p[1]]]
    d2 <- rep_list[[p[2]]]

    models <- c("base", "spa", "pee")

    # Compute GEER for each model
    pair_res <- lapply(models, function(m) {
      
      g1 <- get_gblup_yld2_et23(d1, m, grm_inverse)
      g2 <- get_gblup_yld2_et23(d2, m, grm_inverse)

      # Skip if either replicate failed
      if (is.null(g1) || is.null(g2)) return(NULL)

      # Align common germplasm entries
      common_ids <- intersect(names(g1), names(g2))
      if (length(common_ids) < 2) return(NULL)

      # Compute correlations
      pear <- tryCatch(
        cor(g1[common_ids], g2[common_ids]),
        error = function(e) NA_real_
      )
      
      spear <- tryCatch(
        cor(g1[common_ids], g2[common_ids], method = "spearman"),
        error = function(e) NA_real_
      )

      # Return results
      data.frame(
        Rep1 = p[1],
        Rep2 = p[2],
        Model = m,
        N_common = length(common_ids),
        Pearson = pear,
        Spearman = spear,
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      )
    })

    do.call(rbind, pair_res)
  })

  # Combine all results
  res <- do.call(rbind, res)
  rownames(res) <- NULL

  return(res)
}


### ---------------------------------------------------------
### 3. Run GEER analysis
### ---------------------------------------------------------
GEER_results_yld2_et23 <- geer_all_pairs_yld2_et23(
  nmsu23_et_pheno,
  grm_inverse
)

GEER_results_yld2_et23


### ---------------------------------------------------------
### 4. Summary statistics
### ---------------------------------------------------------

# Number of valid comparisons per model
table(GEER_results_yld2_et23$Model)

# Mean GEER per model
aggregate(
  cbind(Pearson, Spearman) ~ Model,
  GEER_results_yld2_et23,
  mean
)


### ---------------------------------------------------------
### 5. Visualization: GEER (Pearson)
### ---------------------------------------------------------

# Ensure consistent ordering for plotting
GEER_results_yld2_et23$Model <- factor(
  GEER_results_yld2_et23$Model,
  levels = c("base", "spa", "pee"),
  labels = c("Base", "Spa(AR)", "PEE"))

# Boxplot of Pearson GEER
boxplot(
  Pearson ~ Model,
  data = GEER_results_yld2_et23,
  col = c("grey70", "skyblue", "tomato"),
  border = "black",
  ylab = "GEER (Pearson correlation)",
  xlab = "Model",
  main = "Genotypic Effect Estimation across Replicates (GEER)\nHarvest 2, et 2023",
  outline = TRUE
)

# Overlay individual replicate-pair estimates
stripchart(
  Pearson ~ Model,
  data = GEER_results_yld2_et23,
  vertical = TRUE,
  method = "jitter",
  pch = 19,
  col = "black",
  add = TRUE
)
```

###  Spatially Corrected Rep-wise Yield Correlation (SCRYC)
 - correlation of phenotypes/yield after removing spatial effects across reps
- PEE much better cz autoreg.is not capturing
```{r  Spatially Corrected Yiled, Yld2, 04272026}
# ============================================================
# NEW METRIC: SPATIALLY CORRECTED YIELD (yld2_et23)
# ============================================================

# -------------------------------
# 1. PREPARE WORKING DATA
# -------------------------------
nmsu23_et_pheno_SC <- nmsu23_et_pheno

# ============================================================
# 1.1 SPATIAL (AR1): EXTRACT + ALIGN SPATIAL BLUPS
# ============================================================

# Extract all random effects
spa_blup_yld2_et23 <- uni_nmsu23_et_yld2_spa$coefficients$random
spa_blup_yld2_et23
# Extract ONLY Row:Range spatial effects (correct pattern)
spa_eff_yld2_et23 <- spa_blup_yld2_et23[
  grep("^Row_[0-9]+:Range_[0-9]+", rownames(spa_blup_yld2_et23)),
  , drop = FALSE]
spa_eff_yld2_et23

# Build lookup table (use column name "effect")
spa_df_yld2_et23 <- data.frame(
  RowRange = rownames(spa_eff_yld2_et23),
  spa_eff_yld2_et23 = spa_eff_yld2_et23[,"effect"],
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
spa_df_yld2_et23
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Create matching key in phenotype data
# ------------------------------------------------------------
nmsu23_et_pheno_SC$RowRange <- paste0(
  "Row_", nmsu23_et_pheno_SC$Row,
  ":Range_", nmsu23_et_pheno_SC$Range)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Match WITHOUT reordering (IMPORTANT)
# ------------------------------------------------------------

match_idx <- match(
  nmsu23_et_pheno_SC$RowRange,
  spa_df_yld2_et23$RowRange)

nmsu23_et_pheno_SC$spa_eff_yld2_et23 <- 
  spa_df_yld2_et23$spa_eff_yld2_et23[match_idx]
 # i doubled check the spatial blups and these columns to make sure i am getting what i wanted

# Sanity check (must be zero)
sum(is.na(nmsu23_et_pheno_SC$spa_eff_yld2_et23)) # 0

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Corrected yield (AR1)
# ------------------------------------------------------------

nmsu23_et_pheno_SC$yld2_spa_corr_et23 <- 
  nmsu23_et_pheno_SC$yld2 - nmsu23_et_pheno_SC$spa_eff_yld2_et23




# ============================================================
# 1.2 PEE: DIRECT SPATIAL CORRECTION
# ============================================================

 # we need to scale PEE to be able to use it for spatial correction

# lets see
# Extract coefficient
beta_pee_yld2_et23 <- uni_nmsu23_et_yld2_pee$coefficients$fixed["PEE_153", "effect"]
beta_pee_yld2_et23   #  

# Apply correct spatial correction
nmsu23_et_pheno_SC$yld2_pee_corr_et23 <- 
  nmsu23_et_pheno_SC$yld2 - 
  beta_pee_yld2_et23 * nmsu23_et_pheno_SC$PEE_153


# ============================================================
# 2. REP-WISE CORRELATIONS
# ============================================================

# -------------------------------
# SPLIT DATA BY REP
# -------------------------------

rep1_yld2_et23 <- nmsu23_et_pheno_SC[nmsu23_et_pheno_SC$Rep == 1, ]
dim(nmsu23_et_pheno_SC) # 144*60
dim(rep1_yld2_et23) # should be 144/4 = 36 and it is. JUST SANITY CHECK
rep2_yld2_et23 <- nmsu23_et_pheno_SC[nmsu23_et_pheno_SC$Rep == 2, ]
rep3_yld2_et23 <- nmsu23_et_pheno_SC[nmsu23_et_pheno_SC$Rep == 3, ]
rep4_yld2_et23 <- nmsu23_et_pheno_SC[nmsu23_et_pheno_SC$Rep == 4, ]

# Align by genotype
rep1_yld2_et23 <- rep1_yld2_et23[order(rep1_yld2_et23$Germplasm), ]
rep2_yld2_et23 <- rep2_yld2_et23[order(rep2_yld2_et23$Germplasm), ]
rep3_yld2_et23 <- rep3_yld2_et23[order(rep3_yld2_et23$Germplasm), ]
rep4_yld2_et23 <- rep4_yld2_et23[order(rep4_yld2_et23$Germplasm), ]


# ============================================================
# 1. RAW YIELD
# ============================================================

cor_raw_yld2_et23 <- c(
  cor(rep1_yld2_et23$yld2, rep2_yld2_et23$yld2, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep1_yld2_et23$yld2, rep3_yld2_et23$yld2, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep1_yld2_et23$yld2, rep4_yld2_et23$yld2, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep2_yld2_et23$yld2, rep3_yld2_et23$yld2, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep2_yld2_et23$yld2, rep4_yld2_et23$yld2, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep3_yld2_et23$yld2, rep4_yld2_et23$yld2, use="complete.obs") )

df_raw_yld2_et23 <- data.frame(
  Model = "Raw",
  Correlation = cor_raw_yld2_et23)
df_raw_yld2_et23

# ============================================================
# 2. AR1 CORRECTED
# ============================================================

cor_spa_cor_yld2_et23 <- c(
  cor(rep1_yld2_et23$yld2_spa_corr_et23, rep2_yld2_et23$yld2_spa_corr_et23, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep1_yld2_et23$yld2_spa_corr_et23, rep3_yld2_et23$yld2_spa_corr_et23, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep1_yld2_et23$yld2_spa_corr_et23, rep4_yld2_et23$yld2_spa_corr_et23, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep2_yld2_et23$yld2_spa_corr_et23, rep3_yld2_et23$yld2_spa_corr_et23, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep2_yld2_et23$yld2_spa_corr_et23, rep4_yld2_et23$yld2_spa_corr_et23, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep3_yld2_et23$yld2_spa_corr_et23, rep4_yld2_et23$yld2_spa_corr_et23, use="complete.obs"))

df_spa_yld2_et23 <- data.frame(
  Model = "Spa(AR1)",
  Correlation = cor_spa_cor_yld2_et23)
df_spa_yld2_et23

# ============================================================
# 3. PEE CORRECTED
# ============================================================

cor_pee_cor_yld2_et23 <- c(
  cor(rep1_yld2_et23$yld2_pee_corr_et23, rep2_yld2_et23$yld2_pee_corr_et23, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep1_yld2_et23$yld2_pee_corr_et23, rep3_yld2_et23$yld2_pee_corr_et23, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep1_yld2_et23$yld2_pee_corr_et23, rep4_yld2_et23$yld2_pee_corr_et23, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep2_yld2_et23$yld2_pee_corr_et23, rep3_yld2_et23$yld2_pee_corr_et23, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep2_yld2_et23$yld2_pee_corr_et23, rep4_yld2_et23$yld2_pee_corr_et23, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep3_yld2_et23$yld2_pee_corr_et23, rep4_yld2_et23$yld2_pee_corr_et23, use="complete.obs"))

df_pee_yld2_et23 <- data.frame(
  Model = "PEE",
  Correlation = cor_pee_cor_yld2_et23)
df_pee_yld2_et23

# ============================================================
# 4. COMBINE + PLOT
# ============================================================

df_all_yld2_et23 <- rbind(
  df_raw_yld2_et23,
  df_spa_yld2_et23,
  df_pee_yld2_et23)

df_all_yld2_et23$Model <- factor(
  df_all_yld2_et23$Model,
  levels = c("Raw", "Spa(AR1)", "PEE"))

boxplot(
  Correlation ~ Model,
  data = df_all_yld2_et23,
  col = c("lightgray", "lightblue", "lightgreen"),
  ylab = "Rep-to-rep correlation",
  main = "ET23 yld2: Spatial Correction Comparison",
  ylim = c(0,1)
)

# Summary
aggregate(Correlation ~ Model, df_all_yld2_et23, mean)
aggregate(Correlation ~ Model, df_all_yld2_et23, sd)
```

- 1. Using Random regression

-NOTE: Check yld#, harvest #, PEE
- for RR, had to simplify model to run it. 

```{r Combined chunk for Harvest 3 using Random Regression 04282026}
# ---------- PART 0: Manange data file -----------

#  Manage data file: First, assign harvest based on GDD
# first make Harvest 3 only data file
nmsu23_et_pheno_gndvi_only_long_harvestwise <- 
  nmsu23_et_pheno_gndvi_only_long %>%
  mutate(Harvest = case_when(
    # no harvest 1 in this year
    GDD >= 119 & GDD <= 153 ~ "Harvest2", # here upper limit is of actual yld
    GDD >= 153 & GDD <= 182 ~ "Harvest3",
    GDD >= 181 & GDD <= 208 ~ "Harvest4",
    GDD >= 207 & GDD <= 279 ~ "Harvest5",
    GDD >= 243 & GDD <= 311 ~ "Harvest6"))

# Subset harvest3
nmsu23_et_gdd_harvest3 <- nmsu23_et_pheno_gndvi_only_long_harvestwise %>%
  filter(Harvest == "Harvest3") # !!! capital H

# create factor + numeric GDD
nmsu23_et_gdd_harvest3$GDD_fac <- as.factor(nmsu23_et_gdd_harvest3$GDD)
nmsu23_et_gdd_harvest3 <- nmsu23_et_gdd_harvest3[order(nmsu23_et_gdd_harvest3$GDD_fac),]

unique(nmsu23_et_gdd_harvest3$GDD_fac) # 160 165 173 179 182(for yld3)

# Build Legendre basis
unique_gdd_yld3 <- sort(unique(nmsu23_et_gdd_harvest3$GDD))
unique_gdd_yld3 <- as.numeric(unique_gdd_yld3)

 ######## fitting linear equation
M_yld3 <- stdtime(unique_gdd_yld3, 1) # for linear, 1
lambda_yld3 <- Legendre(1, gengler=TRUE) # for linear, 1 (intercept + slope)

Phi_yld3 <- M_yld3 %*% t(lambda_yld3)
colnames(Phi_yld3) <- c("LPInt", "LPLin")
rownames(Phi_yld3) <- unique_gdd_yld3
Phi_yld3
ordLP_yld3 <- match(nmsu23_et_gdd_harvest3$GDD, rownames(Phi_yld3))
nmsu23_et_gdd_harvest3$LPInt_yld3 <- Phi_yld3[ordLP_yld3, "LPInt"]
nmsu23_et_gdd_harvest3$LPLin_yld3 <- Phi_yld3[ordLP_yld3, "LPLin"]

# Fit RR model (harvest3)
asreml.options(extra = 200, maxit = 200)

lp_mod_et_23_yld3 <- { 
  attr(grm_inverse, "INVERSE") <- TRUE
  asreml(
    fixed = GNDVI ~ 1 + at(GDD_fac):Rep,
    random = ~ str(~ Germplasm:LPInt_yld3 + Germplasm:LPLin_yld3, ~ diag(2):vm(Germplasm, grm_inverse)) + str(~ Plot:LPInt_yld3 + Plot:LPLin_yld3, ~ diag(2):id(Plot)), # us didn't work so using diag
    residual = ~ dsum(~ units | GDD_fac),
    data = nmsu23_et_gdd_harvest3)}

summary(lp_mod_et_23_yld3)$varcomp
lp_mod_et_23_yld3 <- update.asreml(lp_mod_et_23_yld3, start = lp_mod_et_23_yld3$gammas)

# Save random effects (BLUPs)
blups_yld3 <- lp_mod_et_23_yld3$coefficients$random
blups_yld3

# --- Convert full BLUPs to a data frame ---
blups_df_yld3 <- as.data.frame(blups_yld3) %>% rename(solution = 1)
blups_df_yld3
# Add term names (simplify)
blups_df_yld3$term <- gsub(":.*", "", rownames(blups_df_yld3))

# --- Filter subsets ---
# BLUP_germplasm_yld3 <- blups_df_yld3 %>% filter(grepl("^Germplasm", rownames(blups_df_yld3)))
```

### 2. GEER
 - NOTE: yld#, PEE_###, Check AR model (full or 1D)

```{r GEER between all rep combinations for yld3 et 2023, 04282026}
### ---------------------------------------------------------
### 1. Function: Fit model and extract genomic BLUPs
### ---------------------------------------------------------
get_gblup_yld3_et23 <- function(dat, model_type = c("base", "spa", "pee"), grm_inverse) {
  
  # Ensure GRM is treated as inverse relationship matrix
  attr(grm_inverse, "INVERSE") <- TRUE
  
  # Match model type argument
  model_type <- match.arg(model_type)

  # ---------------------------------------------------------
  # Fit model (robust to failure)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------
  fit <- tryCatch({
    
    if (model_type == "base") {
      # Baseline genomic model (no spatial/environmental correction)
      asreml(
        fixed   = yld3 ~ 1 , # we dont need rep here cz the data is only for one rep
        random  = ~ vm(Germplasm, grm_inverse),
        residual= ~ id(units),
        data    = dat
      )
      
    } else if (model_type == "spa") {
      # Genomic model + 2D autoregressive spatial structure
      asreml(
        fixed   = yld3 ~ 1 , # we dont need rep here cz the data is only for one rep
        random  = ~ vm(Germplasm, grm_inverse) + ar1(Row):ar1(Range),
        residual= ~ id(units),
        data    = dat
      )
      
    } else if (model_type == "pee") {
      # Genomic model + permanent environmental effect (PEE)
      asreml(
        fixed   = yld3 ~ 1 + PEE_182,
        random  = ~ vm(Germplasm, grm_inverse),
        residual= ~ id(units),
        data    = dat
      )
    }
    
  }, error = function(e) NULL)   # Return NULL if model fails

  # If model fitting failed → skip
  if (is.null(fit)) return(NULL)

  # ---------------------------------------------------------
  # Extract genomic BLUPs (u_a)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------
  blup <- tryCatch(coef(fit)$random, error = function(e) NULL)
  
  # If extraction failed → skip
  if (is.null(blup)) return(NULL)

  # Keep only Germplasm effects
  blup <- blup[grep("Germplasm", rownames(blup)), , drop = FALSE]
  
  # If no genetic effects found → skip
  if (nrow(blup) == 0) return(NULL)

  # Convert to named numeric vector
  out <- blup[, 1]
  names(out) <- rownames(blup)

  return(out)
}


### ---------------------------------------------------------
### 2. Function: Compute GEER across all replicate pairs
### ---------------------------------------------------------
geer_all_pairs_yld3_et23 <- function(dat, grm_inverse, rep_col = "Rep") {
  
  # Split dataset by replicate
  rep_list <- split(dat, dat[[rep_col]])
  rep_names <- names(rep_list)
  
  # All pairwise replicate combinations
  pairs <- combn(rep_names, 2, simplify = FALSE)

  # Loop over replicate pairs
  res <- lapply(pairs, function(p) {
    
    d1 <- rep_list[[p[1]]]
    d2 <- rep_list[[p[2]]]

    models <- c("base", "spa", "pee")

    # Compute GEER for each model
    pair_res <- lapply(models, function(m) {
      
      g1 <- get_gblup_yld3_et23(d1, m, grm_inverse)
      g2 <- get_gblup_yld3_et23(d2, m, grm_inverse)

      # Skip if either replicate failed
      if (is.null(g1) || is.null(g2)) return(NULL)

      # Align common germplasm entries
      common_ids <- intersect(names(g1), names(g2))
      if (length(common_ids) < 2) return(NULL)

      # Compute correlations
      pear <- tryCatch(
        cor(g1[common_ids], g2[common_ids]),
        error = function(e) NA_real_
      )
      
      spear <- tryCatch(
        cor(g1[common_ids], g2[common_ids], method = "spearman"),
        error = function(e) NA_real_
      )

      # Return results
      data.frame(
        Rep1 = p[1],
        Rep2 = p[2],
        Model = m,
        N_common = length(common_ids),
        Pearson = pear,
        Spearman = spear,
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      )
    })

    do.call(rbind, pair_res)
  })

  # Combine all results
  res <- do.call(rbind, res)
  rownames(res) <- NULL

  return(res)
}


### ---------------------------------------------------------
### 3. Run GEER analysis
### ---------------------------------------------------------
GEER_results_yld3_et23 <- geer_all_pairs_yld3_et23(
  nmsu23_et_pheno,
  grm_inverse
)

GEER_results_yld3_et23


### ---------------------------------------------------------
### 4. Summary statistics
### ---------------------------------------------------------

# Number of valid comparisons per model
table(GEER_results_yld3_et23$Model)

# Mean GEER per model
aggregate(
  cbind(Pearson, Spearman) ~ Model,
  GEER_results_yld3_et23,
  mean
)


### ---------------------------------------------------------
### 5. Visualization: GEER (Pearson)
### ---------------------------------------------------------

# Ensure consistent ordering for plotting
GEER_results_yld3_et23$Model <- factor(
  GEER_results_yld3_et23$Model,
  levels = c("base", "spa", "pee"),
  labels = c("Base", "Spa(AR)", "PEE"))

# Boxplot of Pearson GEER
boxplot(
  Pearson ~ Model,
  data = GEER_results_yld3_et23,
  col = c("grey70", "skyblue", "tomato"),
  border = "black",
  ylab = "GEER (Pearson correlation)",
  xlab = "Model",
  main = "Genotypic Effect Estimation across Replicates (GEER)\nHarvest 3, et 2023",
  outline = TRUE
)

# Overlay individual replicate-pair estimates
stripchart(
  Pearson ~ Model,
  data = GEER_results_yld3_et23,
  vertical = TRUE,
  method = "jitter",
  pch = 19,
  col = "black",
  add = TRUE
)
```

###  Spatially Corrected Rep-wise Yield Correlation (SCRYC)
 - correlation of phenotypes/yield after removing spatial effects across reps

```{r  Spatially Corrected Yiled, yld3, 04282026}
# ============================================================
# NEW METRIC: SPATIALLY CORRECTED YIELD (yld3_et23)
# ============================================================

# -------------------------------
# 1. PREPARE WORKING DATA
# -------------------------------
nmsu23_et_pheno_SC <- nmsu23_et_pheno

# ============================================================
# 1.1 SPATIAL (AR1): EXTRACT + ALIGN SPATIAL BLUPS
# ============================================================

# Extract all random effects
spa_blup_yld3_et23 <- uni_nmsu23_et_yld3_spa$coefficients$random
spa_blup_yld3_et23
# Extract ONLY Row:Range spatial effects (correct pattern)
spa_eff_yld3_et23 <- spa_blup_yld3_et23[
  grep("^Row_[0-9]+:Range_[0-9]+", rownames(spa_blup_yld3_et23)),
  , drop = FALSE]
spa_eff_yld3_et23

# Build lookup table (use column name "effect")
spa_df_yld3_et23 <- data.frame(
  RowRange = rownames(spa_eff_yld3_et23),
  spa_eff_yld3_et23 = spa_eff_yld3_et23[,"effect"],
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
spa_df_yld3_et23
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Create matching key in phenotype data
# ------------------------------------------------------------
nmsu23_et_pheno_SC$RowRange <- paste0(
  "Row_", nmsu23_et_pheno_SC$Row,
  ":Range_", nmsu23_et_pheno_SC$Range)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Match WITHOUT reordering (IMPORTANT)
# ------------------------------------------------------------

match_idx <- match(
  nmsu23_et_pheno_SC$RowRange,
  spa_df_yld3_et23$RowRange)

nmsu23_et_pheno_SC$spa_eff_yld3_et23 <- 
  spa_df_yld3_et23$spa_eff_yld3_et23[match_idx]
 # i doubled check the spatial blups and these columns to make sure i am getting what i wanted

# Sanity check (must be zero)
sum(is.na(nmsu23_et_pheno_SC$spa_eff_yld3_et23)) # 0

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Corrected yield (AR1)
# ------------------------------------------------------------

nmsu23_et_pheno_SC$yld3_spa_corr_et23 <- 
  nmsu23_et_pheno_SC$yld3 - nmsu23_et_pheno_SC$spa_eff_yld3_et23




# ============================================================
# 1.2 PEE: DIRECT SPATIAL CORRECTION
# ============================================================

 # we need to scale PEE to be able to use it for spatial correction

# lets see
# Extract coefficient
beta_pee_yld3_et23 <- uni_nmsu23_et_yld3_pee$coefficients$fixed["PEE_182", "effect"]
beta_pee_yld3_et23   #  

# Apply correct spatial correction
nmsu23_et_pheno_SC$yld3_pee_corr_et23 <- 
  nmsu23_et_pheno_SC$yld3 - 
  beta_pee_yld3_et23 * nmsu23_et_pheno_SC$PEE_182


# ============================================================
# 2. REP-WISE CORRELATIONS
# ============================================================

# -------------------------------
# SPLIT DATA BY REP
# -------------------------------

rep1_yld3_et23 <- nmsu23_et_pheno_SC[nmsu23_et_pheno_SC$Rep == 1, ]
dim(nmsu23_et_pheno_SC) # 144*60
dim(rep1_yld3_et23) # should be 144/4 = 36 and it is. JUST SANITY CHECK
rep2_yld3_et23 <- nmsu23_et_pheno_SC[nmsu23_et_pheno_SC$Rep == 2, ]
rep3_yld3_et23 <- nmsu23_et_pheno_SC[nmsu23_et_pheno_SC$Rep == 3, ]
rep4_yld3_et23 <- nmsu23_et_pheno_SC[nmsu23_et_pheno_SC$Rep == 4, ]

# Align by genotype
rep1_yld3_et23 <- rep1_yld3_et23[order(rep1_yld3_et23$Germplasm), ]
rep2_yld3_et23 <- rep2_yld3_et23[order(rep2_yld3_et23$Germplasm), ]
rep3_yld3_et23 <- rep3_yld3_et23[order(rep3_yld3_et23$Germplasm), ]
rep4_yld3_et23 <- rep4_yld3_et23[order(rep4_yld3_et23$Germplasm), ]


# ============================================================
# 1. RAW YIELD
# ============================================================

cor_raw_yld3_et23 <- c(
  cor(rep1_yld3_et23$yld3, rep2_yld3_et23$yld3, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep1_yld3_et23$yld3, rep3_yld3_et23$yld3, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep1_yld3_et23$yld3, rep4_yld3_et23$yld3, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep2_yld3_et23$yld3, rep3_yld3_et23$yld3, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep2_yld3_et23$yld3, rep4_yld3_et23$yld3, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep3_yld3_et23$yld3, rep4_yld3_et23$yld3, use="complete.obs") )

df_raw_yld3_et23 <- data.frame(
  Model = "Raw",
  Correlation = cor_raw_yld3_et23)
df_raw_yld3_et23

# ============================================================
# 2. AR1 CORRECTED
# ============================================================

cor_spa_cor_yld3_et23 <- c(
  cor(rep1_yld3_et23$yld3_spa_corr_et23, rep2_yld3_et23$yld3_spa_corr_et23, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep1_yld3_et23$yld3_spa_corr_et23, rep3_yld3_et23$yld3_spa_corr_et23, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep1_yld3_et23$yld3_spa_corr_et23, rep4_yld3_et23$yld3_spa_corr_et23, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep2_yld3_et23$yld3_spa_corr_et23, rep3_yld3_et23$yld3_spa_corr_et23, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep2_yld3_et23$yld3_spa_corr_et23, rep4_yld3_et23$yld3_spa_corr_et23, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep3_yld3_et23$yld3_spa_corr_et23, rep4_yld3_et23$yld3_spa_corr_et23, use="complete.obs"))

df_spa_yld3_et23 <- data.frame(
  Model = "Spa(AR1)",
  Correlation = cor_spa_cor_yld3_et23)
df_spa_yld3_et23

# ============================================================
# 3. PEE CORRECTED
# ============================================================

cor_pee_cor_yld3_et23 <- c(
  cor(rep1_yld3_et23$yld3_pee_corr_et23, rep2_yld3_et23$yld3_pee_corr_et23, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep1_yld3_et23$yld3_pee_corr_et23, rep3_yld3_et23$yld3_pee_corr_et23, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep1_yld3_et23$yld3_pee_corr_et23, rep4_yld3_et23$yld3_pee_corr_et23, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep2_yld3_et23$yld3_pee_corr_et23, rep3_yld3_et23$yld3_pee_corr_et23, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep2_yld3_et23$yld3_pee_corr_et23, rep4_yld3_et23$yld3_pee_corr_et23, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep3_yld3_et23$yld3_pee_corr_et23, rep4_yld3_et23$yld3_pee_corr_et23, use="complete.obs"))

df_pee_yld3_et23 <- data.frame(
  Model = "PEE",

# ============================================================

df_all_yld3_et23 <- rbind(

boxplot(
```

```{r Combined chunk for Harvest 4 using Random Regression 04282026}
# ---------- PART 0: Manange data file -----------

#  Manage data file: First, assign harvest based on GDD
# first make Harvest 4 only data file
nmsu23_et_pheno_gndvi_only_long_harvestwise <- 
  nmsu23_et_pheno_gndvi_only_long %>%
  mutate(Harvest = case_when(
    # no harvest 1 in this year
    GDD >= 119 & GDD <= 153 ~ "harvest2", # here upper limit is of actual yld
    GDD >= 153 & GDD <= 182 ~ "Harvest3",
    GDD >= 181 & GDD <= 208 ~ "Harvest4",
    GDD >= 207 & GDD <= 279 ~ "Harvest5",
    GDD >= 243 & GDD <= 311 ~ "Harvest6"))

# Subset harvest4
nmsu23_et_gdd_harvest4 <- nmsu23_et_pheno_gndvi_only_long_harvestwise %>%
  filter(Harvest == "Harvest4") # !!! capital H

# create factor + numeric GDD
nmsu23_et_gdd_harvest4$GDD_fac <- as.factor(nmsu23_et_gdd_harvest4$GDD)
nmsu23_et_gdd_harvest4 <- nmsu23_et_gdd_harvest4[order(nmsu23_et_gdd_harvest4$GDD_fac),]

unique(nmsu23_et_gdd_harvest4$GDD_fac) # 192 201 206 208(for yld4)

# Build Legendre basis
unique_gdd_yld4 <- sort(unique(nmsu23_et_gdd_harvest4$GDD))
unique_gdd_yld4 <- as.numeric(unique_gdd_yld4)

 ######## fitting linear equation
M_yld4 <- stdtime(unique_gdd_yld4, 1) # for linear, 1
lambda_yld4 <- Legendre(1, gengler=TRUE) # for linear, 1 (intercept + slope)

Phi_yld4 <- M_yld4 %*% t(lambda_yld4)
colnames(Phi_yld4) <- c("LPInt", "LPLin")
rownames(Phi_yld4) <- unique_gdd_yld4
Phi_yld4
ordLP_yld4 <- match(nmsu23_et_gdd_harvest4$GDD, rownames(Phi_yld4))
nmsu23_et_gdd_harvest4$LPInt_yld4 <- Phi_yld4[ordLP_yld4, "LPInt"]
nmsu23_et_gdd_harvest4$LPLin_yld4 <- Phi_yld4[ordLP_yld4, "LPLin"]

# Fit RR model (harvest4)
asreml.options(extra = 200, maxit = 200)

lp_mod_et_23_yld4 <- { 
  attr(grm_inverse, "INVERSE") <- TRUE
  asreml(
    fixed = GNDVI ~ 1 + at(GDD_fac):Rep,
    random = ~ str(~ Germplasm:LPInt_yld4 + Germplasm:LPLin_yld4, ~ us(2):vm(Germplasm, grm_inverse)) + str(~ Plot:LPInt_yld4 + Plot:LPLin_yld4, ~ diag(2):id(Plot)), # # for quadratic, us(3) # diag for plot
    residual = ~ dsum(~ units | GDD_fac),
    data = nmsu23_et_gdd_harvest4)}

summary(lp_mod_et_23_yld4)$varcomp
lp_mod_et_23_yld4 <- update.asreml(lp_mod_et_23_yld4, start = lp_mod_et_23_yld4$gammas)

# Save random effects (BLUPs)
blups_yld4 <- lp_mod_et_23_yld4$coefficients$random
blups_yld4

# --- Convert full BLUPs to a data frame ---
blups_df_yld4 <- as.data.frame(blups_yld4) %>% rename(solution = 1)
blups_df_yld4
# Add term names (simplify)
blups_df_yld4$term <- gsub(":.*", "", rownames(blups_df_yld4))

# --- Filter subsets ---
# BLUP_germplasm_yld4 <- blups_df_yld4 %>% filter(grepl("^Germplasm", rownames(blups_df_yld4)))
BLUP_spa_int_yld4 <- blups_df_yld4 %>% 
  filter(grepl("^Plot_.*LPInt_yld4$", rownames(blups_df_yld4)))

BLUP_spa_slp_yld4 <- blups_df_yld4 %>% 
  filter(grepl("^Plot_.*LPLin_yld4$", rownames(blups_df_yld4)))

# --- Spatial BLUPs ---
BLUP_spa_int_yld4$solution   # Intercepts
BLUP_spa_slp_yld4$solution   # Slopes

# --- Combine intercept and slope into a matrix ---
spa_BLUP_matrix_yld4 <- cbind(
  BLUP_spa_int_yld4$solution, 
  BLUP_spa_slp_yld4$solution)
spa_BLUP_matrix_yld4

# ---------- Extract spatial BLUPs as PEE (Permanent Environmental Effects) ----------

# Convert matrix into a data frame for including it in the model below cz my model expects columns in the data frame
nmsu23_et_spa_yld4 <- as.data.frame(spa_BLUP_matrix_yld4)
# add these as columns in my data file
nmsu23_et_pheno$spa_int_yld4 <- nmsu23_et_spa_yld4[,1]
nmsu23_et_pheno$spa_slp_yld4 <- nmsu23_et_spa_yld4[,2]

# !!!!!!!!!!!!!!! Permanent Environmental Effect !!!!!!!!!!!!! 
Phi_yld4
# here intercept and slope for GDD on 153 are 1 and 1.7320508 
nmsu23_et_pheno$PEE_208 <- 
  1 * nmsu23_et_pheno$spa_int_yld4 +
  1.7320508 * nmsu23_et_pheno$spa_slp_yld4


# ---------- Step 2: Fit PEE's as fixed regressor on a yield model with spatial correction ----------

# Fit single-trait model for yield (yld4)
# Spatial effects are included as fixed covariates (PEE correction)
uni_nmsu23_et_yld4_pee <- { 
  attr(grm_inverse, "INVERSE") <- TRUE
  asreml(

    residual= ~ id(units),
    data    = nmsu23_et_pheno)}
```

### 2. GEER
 - NOTE: yld#, PEE_###, Check AR model (full or 1D)

```{r GEER between all rep combinations for yld4 et 2023, 04282026}
### ---------------------------------------------------------
### 1. Function: Fit model and extract genomic BLUPs
### ---------------------------------------------------------
get_gblup_yld4_et23 <- function(dat, model_type = c("base", "spa", "pee"), grm_inverse) {
  
  # Ensure GRM is treated as inverse relationship matrix
  attr(grm_inverse, "INVERSE") <- TRUE
  
  # Match model type argument
  model_type <- match.arg(model_type)

  # ---------------------------------------------------------
  # Fit model (robust to failure)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------
  fit <- tryCatch({
    
    if (model_type == "base") {
      # Baseline genomic model (no spatial/environmental correction)
      asreml(
        fixed   = yld4 ~ 1 , # we dont need rep here cz the data is only for one rep
        random  = ~ vm(Germplasm, grm_inverse),
        residual= ~ id(units),
        data    = dat
      )
      
    } else if (model_type == "spa") {
      # Genomic model + 2D autoregressive spatial structure
      asreml(
        fixed   = yld4 ~ 1 , # we dont need rep here cz the data is only for one rep
        random  = ~ vm(Germplasm, grm_inverse) + ar1(Row):ar1(Range),
        residual= ~ id(units),
        data    = dat
      )
      
    } else if (model_type == "pee") {
      # Genomic model + permanent environmental effect (PEE)
      asreml(
        fixed   = yld4 ~ 1 + PEE_208,
        random  = ~ vm(Germplasm, grm_inverse),
        residual= ~ id(units),
        data    = dat
      )
    }
    
  }, error = function(e) NULL)   # Return NULL if model fails

  # If model fitting failed → skip
  if (is.null(fit)) return(NULL)

  # ---------------------------------------------------------
  # Extract genomic BLUPs (u_a)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------
  blup <- tryCatch(coef(fit)$random, error = function(e) NULL)
  
  # If extraction failed → skip
  if (is.null(blup)) return(NULL)

  # Keep only Germplasm effects
  blup <- blup[grep("Germplasm", rownames(blup)), , drop = FALSE]
  
  # If no genetic effects found → skip
  if (nrow(blup) == 0) return(NULL)

  # Convert to named numeric vector
  out <- blup[, 1]
  names(out) <- rownames(blup)

  return(out)
}


### ---------------------------------------------------------
### 2. Function: Compute GEER across all replicate pairs
### ---------------------------------------------------------
geer_all_pairs_yld4_et23 <- function(dat, grm_inverse, rep_col = "Rep") {
  
  # Split dataset by replicate
  rep_list <- split(dat, dat[[rep_col]])
  rep_names <- names(rep_list)
  
  # All pairwise replicate combinations
  pairs <- combn(rep_names, 2, simplify = FALSE)

  # Loop over replicate pairs
  res <- lapply(pairs, function(p) {
    
    d1 <- rep_list[[p[1]]]
    d2 <- rep_list[[p[2]]]

    models <- c("base", "spa", "pee")

    # Compute GEER for each model
    pair_res <- lapply(models, function(m) {
      
      g1 <- get_gblup_yld4_et23(d1, m, grm_inverse)
      g2 <- get_gblup_yld4_et23(d2, m, grm_inverse)

      # Skip if either replicate failed
      if (is.null(g1) || is.null(g2)) return(NULL)

      # Align common germplasm entries
      common_ids <- intersect(names(g1), names(g2))
      if (length(common_ids) < 2) return(NULL)

      # Compute correlations
      pear <- tryCatch(
        cor(g1[common_ids], g2[common_ids]),
        error = function(e) NA_real_
      )
      
      spear <- tryCatch(
        cor(g1[common_ids], g2[common_ids], method = "spearman"),
        error = function(e) NA_real_
      )

      # Return results
      data.frame(
        Rep1 = p[1],
        Rep2 = p[2],
        Model = m,
        N_common = length(common_ids),
        Pearson = pear,
        Spearman = spear,
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      )
    })

    do.call(rbind, pair_res)
  })

  # Combine all results
  res <- do.call(rbind, res)
  rownames(res) <- NULL

  return(res)
}


### ---------------------------------------------------------
### 3. Run GEER analysis
### ---------------------------------------------------------
GEER_results_yld4_et23 <- geer_all_pairs_yld4_et23(
  nmsu23_et_pheno,
  grm_inverse
)

GEER_results_yld4_et23


### ---------------------------------------------------------
### 4. Summary statistics
### ---------------------------------------------------------

# Number of valid comparisons per model
table(GEER_results_yld4_et23$Model)

# Mean GEER per model
aggregate(
  cbind(Pearson, Spearman) ~ Model,
  GEER_results_yld4_et23,
  mean
)


### ---------------------------------------------------------
### 5. Visualization: GEER (Pearson)
### ---------------------------------------------------------

# Ensure consistent ordering for plotting
GEER_results_yld4_et23$Model <- factor(
  GEER_results_yld4_et23$Model,
  levels = c("base", "spa", "pee"),
  labels = c("Base", "Spa(AR)", "PEE"))

# Boxplot of Pearson GEER
boxplot(
  Pearson ~ Model,
  data = GEER_results_yld4_et23,
  col = c("grey70", "skyblue", "tomato"),
  border = "black",
  ylab = "GEER (Pearson correlation)",
  xlab = "Model",
  main = "Genotypic Effect Estimation across Replicates (GEER)\nHarvest 4, et 2023",
  outline = TRUE
)

# Overlay individual replicate-pair estimates
stripchart(
  Pearson ~ Model,
  data = GEER_results_yld4_et23,
  vertical = TRUE,
  method = "jitter",
  pch = 19,
  col = "black",
  add = TRUE
)
```

###  Spatially Corrected Rep-wise Yield Correlation (SCRYC)
 - correlation of phenotypes/yield after removing spatial effects across reps
- PEE much better cz autoreg.is not capturing
```{r  Spatially Corrected Yiled, yld4, 04272026}
# ============================================================
# NEW METRIC: SPATIALLY CORRECTED YIELD (yld4_et23)
# ============================================================

# -------------------------------
# 1. PREPARE WORKING DATA
# -------------------------------
nmsu23_et_pheno_SC <- nmsu23_et_pheno

# ============================================================
# 1.1 SPATIAL (AR1): EXTRACT + ALIGN SPATIAL BLUPS
# ============================================================

# Extract all random effects
spa_blup_yld4_et23 <- uni_nmsu23_et_yld4_spa$coefficients$random
spa_blup_yld4_et23
# Extract ONLY Row:Range spatial effects (correct pattern)
spa_eff_yld4_et23 <- spa_blup_yld4_et23[
  grep("^Row_[0-9]+:Range_[0-9]+", rownames(spa_blup_yld4_et23)),
  , drop = FALSE]
spa_eff_yld4_et23

# Build lookup table (use column name "effect")
spa_df_yld4_et23 <- data.frame(
  RowRange = rownames(spa_eff_yld4_et23),
  spa_eff_yld4_et23 = spa_eff_yld4_et23[,"effect"],
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
spa_df_yld4_et23
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Create matching key in phenotype data
# ------------------------------------------------------------
nmsu23_et_pheno_SC$RowRange <- paste0(
  "Row_", nmsu23_et_pheno_SC$Row,
  ":Range_", nmsu23_et_pheno_SC$Range)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Match WITHOUT reordering (IMPORTANT)
# ------------------------------------------------------------

match_idx <- match(
  nmsu23_et_pheno_SC$RowRange,
  spa_df_yld4_et23$RowRange)

nmsu23_et_pheno_SC$spa_eff_yld4_et23 <- 
  spa_df_yld4_et23$spa_eff_yld4_et23[match_idx]
 # i doubled check the spatial blups and these columns to make sure i am getting what i wanted

# Sanity check (must be zero)
sum(is.na(nmsu23_et_pheno_SC$spa_eff_yld4_et23)) # 0

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Corrected yield (AR1)
# ------------------------------------------------------------

nmsu23_et_pheno_SC$yld4_spa_corr_et23 <- 
  nmsu23_et_pheno_SC$yld4 - nmsu23_et_pheno_SC$spa_eff_yld4_et23




# ============================================================
# 1.2 PEE: DIRECT SPATIAL CORRECTION
# ============================================================

 # we need to scale PEE to be able to use it for spatial correction

# lets see
# Extract coefficient
beta_pee_yld4_et23 <- uni_nmsu23_et_yld4_pee$coefficients$fixed["PEE_208", "effect"]
beta_pee_yld4_et23   #  

# Apply correct spatial correction
nmsu23_et_pheno_SC$yld4_pee_corr_et23 <- 
  nmsu23_et_pheno_SC$yld4 - 
  beta_pee_yld4_et23 * nmsu23_et_pheno_SC$PEE_208


# ============================================================
# 2. REP-WISE CORRELATIONS
# ============================================================

# -------------------------------
# SPLIT DATA BY REP
# -------------------------------

rep1_yld4_et23 <- nmsu23_et_pheno_SC[nmsu23_et_pheno_SC$Rep == 1, ]
dim(nmsu23_et_pheno_SC) # 144*60
dim(rep1_yld4_et23) # should be 144/4 = 36 and it is. JUST SANITY CHECK
rep2_yld4_et23 <- nmsu23_et_pheno_SC[nmsu23_et_pheno_SC$Rep == 2, ]
rep3_yld4_et23 <- nmsu23_et_pheno_SC[nmsu23_et_pheno_SC$Rep == 3, ]
rep4_yld4_et23 <- nmsu23_et_pheno_SC[nmsu23_et_pheno_SC$Rep == 4, ]

# Align by genotype

rep2_yld4_et23 <- rep2_yld4_et23[order(rep2_yld4_et23$Germplasm), ]
rep3_yld4_et23 <- rep3_yld4_et23[order(rep3_yld4_et23$Germplasm), ]
rep4_yld4_et23 <- rep4_yld4_et23[order(rep4_yld4_et23$Germplasm), ]


# ============================================================

cor_raw_yld4_et23 <- c(
  cor(rep1_yld4_et23$yld4, rep2_yld4_et23$yld4, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep1_yld4_et23$yld4, rep3_yld4_et23$yld4, use="complete.obs"),
```

### 2. GEER
 - NOTE: yld#, PEE_###, Check AR model (full or 1D)

```{r GEER between all rep combinations for yld5 et 2023, 04282026}
### ---------------------------------------------------------
### 1. Function: Fit model and extract genomic BLUPs
### ---------------------------------------------------------
get_gblup_yld5_et23 <- function(dat, model_type = c("base", "spa", "pee"), grm_inverse) {
  
  # Ensure GRM is treated as inverse relationship matrix
  attr(grm_inverse, "INVERSE") <- TRUE
  
  # Match model type argument
  model_type <- match.arg(model_type)

  # ---------------------------------------------------------
  # Fit model (robust to failure)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------
  fit <- tryCatch({
    
    if (model_type == "base") {
      # Baseline genomic model (no spatial/environmental correction)
      asreml(
        fixed   = yld5 ~ 1 , # we dont need rep here cz the data is only for one rep
        random  = ~ vm(Germplasm, grm_inverse),
        residual= ~ id(units),
        data    = dat
      )
      
    } else if (model_type == "spa") {
      # Genomic model + 2D autoregressive spatial structure
      asreml(
        fixed   = yld5 ~ 1 , # we dont need rep here cz the data is only for one rep
        random  = ~ vm(Germplasm, grm_inverse) + ar1(Row):ar1(Range),
        residual= ~ id(units),
        data    = dat
      )
      
    } else if (model_type == "pee") {
      # Genomic model + permanent environmental effect (PEE)
      asreml(
        fixed   = yld5 ~ 1 + PEE_279,
        random  = ~ vm(Germplasm, grm_inverse),
        residual= ~ id(units),
        data    = dat
      )
    }
    
  }, error = function(e) NULL)   # Return NULL if model fails

  # If model fitting failed → skip
  if (is.null(fit)) return(NULL)

  # ---------------------------------------------------------
  # Extract genomic BLUPs (u_a)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------
  blup <- tryCatch(coef(fit)$random, error = function(e) NULL)
  
  # If extraction failed → skip
  if (is.null(blup)) return(NULL)

  # Keep only Germplasm effects
  blup <- blup[grep("Germplasm", rownames(blup)), , drop = FALSE]
  
  # If no genetic effects found → skip
  if (nrow(blup) == 0) return(NULL)

  # Convert to named numeric vector
  out <- blup[, 1]
  names(out) <- rownames(blup)

  return(out)
}


### ---------------------------------------------------------
### 2. Function: Compute GEER across all replicate pairs
### ---------------------------------------------------------
geer_all_pairs_yld5_et23 <- function(dat, grm_inverse, rep_col = "Rep") {
  
  # Split dataset by replicate
  rep_list <- split(dat, dat[[rep_col]])
  rep_names <- names(rep_list)
  
  # All pairwise replicate combinations
  pairs <- combn(rep_names, 2, simplify = FALSE)

  # Loop over replicate pairs
  res <- lapply(pairs, function(p) {
    
    d1 <- rep_list[[p[1]]]
    d2 <- rep_list[[p[2]]]

    models <- c("base", "spa", "pee")

    # Compute GEER for each model
    pair_res <- lapply(models, function(m) {
      
      g1 <- get_gblup_yld5_et23(d1, m, grm_inverse)
      g2 <- get_gblup_yld5_et23(d2, m, grm_inverse)

      # Skip if either replicate failed
      if (is.null(g1) || is.null(g2)) return(NULL)

      # Align common germplasm entries
      common_ids <- intersect(names(g1), names(g2))
      if (length(common_ids) < 2) return(NULL)

      # Compute correlations
      pear <- tryCatch(
        cor(g1[common_ids], g2[common_ids]),
        error = function(e) NA_real_
      )
      
      spear <- tryCatch(
        cor(g1[common_ids], g2[common_ids], method = "spearman"),
        error = function(e) NA_real_
      )

      # Return results
      data.frame(
        Rep1 = p[1],
        Rep2 = p[2],
        Model = m,
        N_common = length(common_ids),
        Pearson = pear,
        Spearman = spear,
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      )
    })

    do.call(rbind, pair_res)
  })

  # Combine all results
  res <- do.call(rbind, res)
  rownames(res) <- NULL

  return(res)
}


### ---------------------------------------------------------
### 3. Run GEER analysis
### ---------------------------------------------------------
GEER_results_yld5_et23 <- geer_all_pairs_yld5_et23(
  nmsu23_et_pheno,
  grm_inverse
)

GEER_results_yld5_et23


### ---------------------------------------------------------
### 4. Summary statistics
### ---------------------------------------------------------

# Number of valid comparisons per model
table(GEER_results_yld5_et23$Model)

# Mean GEER per model
aggregate(
  cbind(Pearson, Spearman) ~ Model,
  GEER_results_yld5_et23,
  mean
)


### ---------------------------------------------------------
### 5. Visualization: GEER (Pearson)
### ---------------------------------------------------------

# Ensure consistent ordering for plotting
GEER_results_yld5_et23$Model <- factor(
  GEER_results_yld5_et23$Model,
  levels = c("base", "spa", "pee"),
  labels = c("Base", "Spa(AR)", "PEE"))

# Boxplot of Pearson GEER
boxplot(
  Pearson ~ Model,
  data = GEER_results_yld5_et23,
  col = c("grey70", "skyblue", "tomato"),
  border = "black",
  ylab = "GEER (Pearson correlation)",
  xlab = "Model",
  main = "Genotypic Effect Estimation across Replicates (GEER)\nHarvest 5, et 2023",
  outline = TRUE
)

# Overlay individual replicate-pair estimates
stripchart(
  Pearson ~ Model,
  data = GEER_results_yld5_et23,
  vertical = TRUE,
  method = "jitter",
  pch = 19,
  col = "black",
  add = TRUE
)
```

###  Spatially Corrected Rep-wise Yield Correlation (SCRYC)
 - correlation of phenotypes/yield after removing spatial effects across reps
- PEE much better cz autoreg.is not capturing
```{r  Spatially Corrected Yiled, yld5, 04272026}
# ============================================================
# NEW METRIC: SPATIALLY CORRECTED YIELD (yld5_et23)
# ============================================================

# -------------------------------
# 1. PREPARE WORKING DATA
# -------------------------------
nmsu23_et_pheno_SC <- nmsu23_et_pheno

# ============================================================
# 1.1 SPATIAL (AR1): EXTRACT + ALIGN SPATIAL BLUPS
# ============================================================

# Extract all random effects
spa_blup_yld5_et23 <- uni_nmsu23_et_yld5_spa$coefficients$random
spa_blup_yld5_et23
# Extract ONLY Row:Range spatial effects (correct pattern)
spa_eff_yld5_et23 <- spa_blup_yld5_et23[
  grep("^Row_[0-9]+:Range_[0-9]+", rownames(spa_blup_yld5_et23)),
  , drop = FALSE]
spa_eff_yld5_et23

# Build lookup table (use column name "effect")
spa_df_yld5_et23 <- data.frame(
  RowRange = rownames(spa_eff_yld5_et23),
  spa_eff_yld5_et23 = spa_eff_yld5_et23[,"effect"],
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
spa_df_yld5_et23
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Create matching key in phenotype data
# ------------------------------------------------------------
nmsu23_et_pheno_SC$RowRange <- paste0(
  "Row_", nmsu23_et_pheno_SC$Row,
  ":Range_", nmsu23_et_pheno_SC$Range)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Match WITHOUT reordering (IMPORTANT)
# ------------------------------------------------------------

match_idx <- match(
  nmsu23_et_pheno_SC$RowRange,
  spa_df_yld5_et23$RowRange)

nmsu23_et_pheno_SC$spa_eff_yld5_et23 <- 
  spa_df_yld5_et23$spa_eff_yld5_et23[match_idx]
 # i doubled check the spatial blups and these columns to make sure i am getting what i wanted

# Sanity check (must be zero)
sum(is.na(nmsu23_et_pheno_SC$spa_eff_yld5_et23)) # 0

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Corrected yield (AR1)
# ------------------------------------------------------------

nmsu23_et_pheno_SC$yld5_spa_corr_et23 <- 
  nmsu23_et_pheno_SC$yld5 - nmsu23_et_pheno_SC$spa_eff_yld5_et23




# ============================================================
# 1.2 PEE: DIRECT SPATIAL CORRECTION
# ============================================================

 # we need to scale PEE to be able to use it for spatial correction

# lets see
# Extract coefficient
beta_pee_yld5_et23 <- uni_nmsu23_et_yld5_pee$coefficients$fixed["PEE_279", "effect"]
beta_pee_yld5_et23   #  

# Apply correct spatial correction
nmsu23_et_pheno_SC$yld5_pee_corr_et23 <- 
  nmsu23_et_pheno_SC$yld5 - 
  beta_pee_yld5_et23 * nmsu23_et_pheno_SC$PEE_279


# ============================================================
# 2. REP-WISE CORRELATIONS
# ============================================================

# -------------------------------
# SPLIT DATA BY REP
# -------------------------------

rep1_yld5_et23 <- nmsu23_et_pheno_SC[nmsu23_et_pheno_SC$Rep == 1, ]
dim(nmsu23_et_pheno_SC) # 144*69
dim(rep1_yld5_et23) # should be 144/4 = 36 and it is. JUST SANITY CHECK
rep2_yld5_et23 <- nmsu23_et_pheno_SC[nmsu23_et_pheno_SC$Rep == 2, ]
rep3_yld5_et23 <- nmsu23_et_pheno_SC[nmsu23_et_pheno_SC$Rep == 3, ]
rep4_yld5_et23 <- nmsu23_et_pheno_SC[nmsu23_et_pheno_SC$Rep == 4, ]

# Align by genotype
rep1_yld5_et23 <- rep1_yld5_et23[order(rep1_yld5_et23$Germplasm), ]
rep2_yld5_et23 <- rep2_yld5_et23[order(rep2_yld5_et23$Germplasm), ]
rep3_yld5_et23 <- rep3_yld5_et23[order(rep3_yld5_et23$Germplasm), ]
rep4_yld5_et23 <- rep4_yld5_et23[order(rep4_yld5_et23$Germplasm), ]


# ============================================================
# 1. RAW YIELD
# ============================================================

cor_raw_yld5_et23 <- c(
  cor(rep1_yld5_et23$yld5, rep2_yld5_et23$yld5, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep1_yld5_et23$yld5, rep3_yld5_et23$yld5, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep1_yld5_et23$yld5, rep4_yld5_et23$yld5, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep2_yld5_et23$yld5, rep3_yld5_et23$yld5, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep2_yld5_et23$yld5, rep4_yld5_et23$yld5, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep3_yld5_et23$yld5, rep4_yld5_et23$yld5, use="complete.obs") )

df_raw_yld5_et23 <- data.frame(
  Model = "Raw",
  Correlation = cor_raw_yld5_et23)
df_raw_yld5_et23

# ============================================================
# 2. AR1 CORRECTED
# ============================================================

cor_spa_cor_yld5_et23 <- c(
  cor(rep1_yld5_et23$yld5_spa_corr_et23, rep2_yld5_et23$yld5_spa_corr_et23, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep1_yld5_et23$yld5_spa_corr_et23, rep3_yld5_et23$yld5_spa_corr_et23, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep1_yld5_et23$yld5_spa_corr_et23, rep4_yld5_et23$yld5_spa_corr_et23, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep2_yld5_et23$yld5_spa_corr_et23, rep3_yld5_et23$yld5_spa_corr_et23, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep2_yld5_et23$yld5_spa_corr_et23, rep4_yld5_et23$yld5_spa_corr_et23, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep3_yld5_et23$yld5_spa_corr_et23, rep4_yld5_et23$yld5_spa_corr_et23, use="complete.obs"))

df_spa_yld5_et23 <- data.frame(
  Model = "Spa(AR1)",
  Correlation = cor_spa_cor_yld5_et23)
df_spa_yld5_et23

# ============================================================
# 3. PEE CORRECTED
# ============================================================

cor_pee_cor_yld5_et23 <- c(
  cor(rep1_yld5_et23$yld5_pee_corr_et23, rep2_yld5_et23$yld5_pee_corr_et23, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep1_yld5_et23$yld5_pee_corr_et23, rep3_yld5_et23$yld5_pee_corr_et23, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep1_yld5_et23$yld5_pee_corr_et23, rep4_yld5_et23$yld5_pee_corr_et23, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep2_yld5_et23$yld5_pee_corr_et23, rep3_yld5_et23$yld5_pee_corr_et23, use="complete.obs"),
  cor(rep2_yld5_et23$yld5_pee_corr_et23, rep4_yld5_et23$yld5_pee_corr_et23, use="complete.obs"),

df_pee_yld5_et23 <- data.frame(

# ============================================================

df_all_yld5_et23 <- rbind(

df_all_yld5_et23$Model <- factor(

boxplot(
```

############################ Harvest 6:############################ 
- 1. Using Random regression

-NOTE: Check yld#, harvest #, PEE
```{r Combined chunk for Harvest 6 using Random Regression 04282026}
# ---------- PART 0: Manange data file -----------

#  Manage data file: First, assign harvest based on GDD
# first make Harvest 6 only data file
nmsu23_et_pheno_gndvi_only_long_harvestwise <- 
  nmsu23_et_pheno_gndvi_only_long %>%
  mutate(Harvest = case_when(
    # no harvest 1 in this year
    GDD >= 119 & GDD <= 153 ~ "Harvest2", # here upper limit is of actual yld
    GDD >= 153 & GDD <= 182 ~ "Harvest3",
    GDD >= 181 & GDD <= 208 ~ "Harvest4",
    GDD >= 207 & GDD <= 279 ~ "Harvest5",
    GDD >= 243 & GDD <= 311 ~ "Harvest6"))

# Subset harvest6
nmsu23_et_gdd_harvest6 <- nmsu23_et_pheno_gndvi_only_long_harvestwise %>%
  filter(Harvest == "Harvest6") # !!! capital H

# create factor + numeric GDD
nmsu23_et_gdd_harvest6$GDD_fac <- as.factor(nmsu23_et_gdd_harvest6$GDD)
nmsu23_et_gdd_harvest6 <- nmsu23_et_gdd_harvest6[order(nmsu23_et_gdd_harvest6$GDD_fac),]

unique(nmsu23_et_gdd_harvest6$GDD_fac) # 293 299 307 311(for yld6)

# Build Legendre basis
unique_gdd_yld6 <- sort(unique(nmsu23_et_gdd_harvest6$GDD))
unique_gdd_yld6 <- as.numeric(unique_gdd_yld6)

 ######## fitting linear equation
M_yld6 <- stdtime(unique_gdd_yld6, 1) # for linear, 1
lambda_yld6 <- Legendre(1, gengler=TRUE) # for linear, 1 (intercept + slope)

Phi_yld6 <- M_yld6 %*% t(lambda_yld6)
colnames(Phi_yld6) <- c("LPInt", "LPLin")
rownames(Phi_yld6) <- unique_gdd_yld6
Phi_yld6
ordLP_yld6 <- match(nmsu23_et_gdd_harvest6$GDD, rownames(Phi_yld6))
nmsu23_et_gdd_harvest6$LPInt_yld6 <- Phi_yld6[ordLP_yld6, "LPInt"]
nmsu23_et_gdd_harvest6$LPLin_yld6 <- Phi_yld6[ordLP_yld6, "LPLin"]

# Fit RR model (harvest6)
asreml.options(extra = 200, maxit = 200)

lp_mod_et_23_yld6 <- { 
  attr(grm_inverse, "INVERSE") <- TRUE
  asreml(
    fixed = GNDVI ~ 1 + at(GDD_fac):Rep,
    random = ~ str(~ Germplasm:LPInt_yld6 + Germplasm:LPLin_yld6, ~ us(2):vm(Germplasm, grm_inverse)) + str(~ Plot:LPInt_yld6 + Plot:LPLin_yld6, ~ us(2):id(Plot)), # # for quadratic, us(3)
    residual = ~ dsum(~ units | GDD_fac),
    data = nmsu23_et_gdd_harvest6)}

summary(lp_mod_et_23_yld6)$varcomp
lp_mod_et_23_yld6 <- update.asreml(lp_mod_et_23_yld6, start = lp_mod_et_23_yld6$gammas)

# Save random effects (BLUPs)
blups_yld6 <- lp_mod_et_23_yld6$coefficients$random
blups_yld6

# --- Convert full BLUPs to a data frame ---
blups_df_yld6 <- as.data.frame(blups_yld6) %>% rename(solution = 1)
blups_df_yld6
# Add term names (simplify)
blups_df_yld6$term <- gsub(":.*", "", rownames(blups_df_yld6))

# --- Filter subsets ---
# BLUP_germplasm_yld6 <- blups_df_yld6 %>% filter(grepl("^Germplasm", rownames(blups_df_yld6)))
BLUP_spa_int_yld6 <- blups_df_yld6 %>% 
  filter(grepl("^Plot_.*LPInt_yld6$", rownames(blups_df_yld6)))

BLUP_spa_slp_yld6 <- blups_df_yld6 %>% 
  filter(grepl("^Plot_.*LPLin_yld6$", rownames(blups_df_yld6)))

# --- Spatial BLUPs ---
BLUP_spa_int_yld6$solution   # Intercepts
BLUP_spa_slp_yld6$solution   # Slopes

# --- Combine intercept and slope into a matrix ---
spa_BLUP_matrix_yld6 <- cbind(
  BLUP_spa_int_yld6$solution, 
  BLUP_spa_slp_yld6$solution)
spa_BLUP_matrix_yld6

# ---------- Extract spatial BLUPs as PEE (Permanent Environmental Effects) ----------

# Convert matrix into a data frame for including it in the model below cz my model expects columns in the data frame
nmsu23_et_spa_yld6 <- as.data.frame(spa_BLUP_matrix_yld6)
# add these as columns in my data file
nmsu23_et_pheno$spa_int_yld6 <- nmsu23_et_spa_yld6[,1]
nmsu23_et_pheno$spa_slp_yld6 <- nmsu23_et_spa_yld6[,2]

# !!!!!!!!!!!!!!! Permanent Environmental Effect !!!!!!!!!!!!! 
Phi_yld6
# here intercept and slope for GDD on PEE_311 are 1 and 1.7320508 
nmsu23_et_pheno$PEE_311 <- 
  1 * nmsu23_et_pheno$spa_int_yld6 +
  1.7320508 * nmsu23_et_pheno$spa_slp_yld6


# ---------- Step 2: Fit PEE's as fixed regressor on a yield model with spatial correction ----------

# Fit single-trait model for yield (yld6)
# Spatial effects are included as fixed covariates (PEE correction)
uni_nmsu23_et_yld6_pee <- { 
  attr(grm_inverse, "INVERSE") <- TRUE
  asreml(
    fixed   = yld6 ~ 1 + Rep + PEE_311,   # PEE as fixed regressors !!!!!!!!!!!! check PEE used
    random  = ~ vm(Germplasm, grm_inverse),         # genomic effect
    residual= ~ id(units),
    data    = nmsu23_et_pheno)}


# Extract variance components
summary(uni_nmsu23_et_yld6_pee)$varcomp




# 1st model: yield alone genetic model without spatial (autoregressive)
uni_nmsu23_et_yld6 <- { 
    attr(grm_inverse, "INVERSE") <- TRUE
  asreml(fixed = yld6 ~ 1 + Rep, #rep effect as fixed
         random = ~ vm(Germplasm, grm_inverse),
         residual = ~ id(units),
         data = nmsu23_et_pheno)}
summary(uni_nmsu23_et_yld6)$varcomp



# 2nd model: yield alone genetic model with spatial (autoregressive)
## Univariate with autoregressive spatial correction
asreml.options(extra = 200, maxit = 200)

uni_nmsu23_et_yld6_spa <- { 
    attr(grm_inverse, "INVERSE") <- TRUE
  asreml(fixed = yld6 ~ 1 + Rep, #rep effect as fixed
         random = ~ vm(Germplasm, grm_inverse) +ar1(Row):ar1(Range),
         residual = ~ id(units),
         data = nmsu23_et_pheno)}
summary(uni_nmsu23_et_yld6_spa)$varcomp


# compare

# variance components
```

### 2. GEER
 - NOTE: yld#, PEE_###, Check AR model (full or 1D)

```{r GEER between all rep combinations for yld6 et 2023, 04282026}
### ---------------------------------------------------------
### 1. Function: Fit model and extract genomic BLUPs
### ---------------------------------------------------------
get_gblup_yld6_et23 <- function(dat, model_type = c("base", "spa", "pee"), grm_inverse) {
  
  # Ensure GRM is treated as inverse relationship matrix
  attr(grm_inverse, "INVERSE") <- TRUE
  
  # Match model type argument
  model_type <- match.arg(model_type)

  # ---------------------------------------------------------
  # Fit model (robust to failure)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------
  fit <- tryCatch({
    
    if (model_type == "base") {
      # Baseline genomic model (no spatial/environmental correction)
      asreml(
        fixed   = yld6 ~ 1 , # we dont need rep here cz the data is only for one rep
        random  = ~ vm(Germplasm, grm_inverse),
        residual= ~ id(units),
        data    = dat
      )
      
    } else if (model_type == "spa") {
      # Genomic model + 2D autoregressive spatial structure
      asreml(
        fixed   = yld6 ~ 1 , # we dont need rep here cz the data is only for one rep
        random  = ~ vm(Germplasm, grm_inverse) + ar1(Row):ar1(Range),
        residual= ~ id(units),
        data    = dat
      )
      
    } else if (model_type == "pee") {
      # Genomic model + permanent environmental effect (PEE)
      asreml(
        fixed   = yld6 ~ 1 + PEE_311,
        random  = ~ vm(Germplasm, grm_inverse),
        residual= ~ id(units),
        data    = dat
      )
    }
    
  }, error = function(e) NULL)   # Return NULL if model fails

  # If model fitting failed → skip
  if (is.null(fit)) return(NULL)

  # ---------------------------------------------------------
  # Extract genomic BLUPs (u_a)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------
  blup <- tryCatch(coef(fit)$random, error = function(e) NULL)
  
  # If extraction failed → skip
  if (is.null(blup)) return(NULL)

  # Keep only Germplasm effects
  blup <- blup[grep("Germplasm", rownames(blup)), , drop = FALSE]
  
  # If no genetic effects found → skip
  if (nrow(blup) == 0) return(NULL)

  # Convert to named numeric vector
  out <- blup[, 1]
  names(out) <- rownames(blup)

  return(out)
}


### ---------------------------------------------------------
### 2. Function: Compute GEER across all replicate pairs
### ---------------------------------------------------------
geer_all_pairs_yld6_et23 <- function(dat, grm_inverse, rep_col = "Rep") {
  
  # Split dataset by replicate
  rep_list <- split(dat, dat[[rep_col]])
  rep_names <- names(rep_list)
  
  # All pairwise replicate combinations
  pairs <- combn(rep_names, 2, simplify = FALSE)

  # Loop over replicate pairs
  res <- lapply(pairs, function(p) {
    
    d1 <- rep_list[[p[1]]]
    d2 <- rep_list[[p[2]]]

    models <- c("base", "spa", "pee")

    # Compute GEER for each model
    pair_res <- lapply(models, function(m) {
      
      g1 <- get_gblup_yld6_et23(d1, m, grm_inverse)
      g2 <- get_gblup_yld6_et23(d2, m, grm_inverse)

      # Skip if either replicate failed
      if (is.null(g1) || is.null(g2)) return(NULL)

      # Align common germplasm entries
      common_ids <- intersect(names(g1), names(g2))
      if (length(common_ids) < 2) return(NULL)

      # Compute correlations
      pear <- tryCatch(
        cor(g1[common_ids], g2[common_ids]),
        error = function(e) NA_real_
      )
      
      spear <- tryCatch(
        cor(g1[common_ids], g2[common_ids], method = "spearman"),
        error = function(e) NA_real_
      )

      # Return results
      data.frame(
        Rep1 = p[1],
        Rep2 = p[2],
        Model = m,
        N_common = length(common_ids),
        Pearson = pear,
        Spearman = spear,
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      )
    })

    do.call(rbind, pair_res)
  })

  # Combine all results
  res <- do.call(rbind, res)
  rownames(res) <- NULL

  return(res)
}


### ---------------------------------------------------------
### 3. Run GEER analysis
### ---------------------------------------------------------
GEER_results_yld6_et23 <- geer_all_pairs_yld6_et23(
  nmsu23_et_pheno,
  grm_inverse
)

GEER_results_yld6_et23


### ---------------------------------------------------------
### 4. Summary statistics
### ---------------------------------------------------------

# Number of valid comparisons per model
table(GEER_results_yld6_et23$Model)

# Mean GEER per model
aggregate(
  cbind(Pearson, Spearman) ~ Model,
  GEER_results_yld6_et23,
  mean
)


### ---------------------------------------------------------
### 5. Visualization: GEER (Pearson)
### ---------------------------------------------------------

# Ensure consistent ordering for plotting
GEER_results_yld6_et23$Model <- factor(
  GEER_results_yld6_et23$Model,
  levels = c("base", "spa", "pee"),
  labels = c("Base", "Spa(AR)", "PEE"))

# Boxplot of Pearson GEER
boxplot(
  Pearson ~ Model,
  data = GEER_results_yld6_et23,
  col = c("grey70", "skyblue", "tomato"),
  border = "black",
  ylab = "GEER (Pearson correlation)",
  xlab = "Model",
  main = "Genotypic Effect Estimation across Replicates (GEER)\nHarvest 6, et 2023",
  outline = TRUE
)

# Overlay individual replicate-pair estimates
stripchart(
  Pearson ~ Model,
  data = GEER_results_yld6_et23,
  vertical = TRUE,
  method = "jitter",
  pch = 19,
  col = "black",
  add = TRUE
)
```
